articles.title: Watch: CCTV shows people take cover after missile strikes hits Riyadh airport
articles.summary:
Footage from inside the airport shows the moment the strike hit on Saturday.

 at Riyadh international airport after strike on SaturdayTwo strikes on the international airport in the Saudi capital of Riyadh have left 14 dead and more than 300 injured.
articles.body:
Two strikes on the international airport in the Saudi capital of Riyadh have left 14 dead and more than 300 injured. There have been a series of other attacks earlier in the week.

CCTV footage from inside King Khalid International Airport shows people taking cover as one of the missiles hit the building on Saturday.

The Houthis in Yemen say they were behind the strikes and warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi Arabian airports and airspace. The group said they had targeted the airport with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones.

They also attacked oil facilities and Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, their military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree said. He vowed to continue the "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia", warning that all Saudi airports were potential targets apart from those in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

articles.title: NI healthcare workers at 'tipping point' as union ballots for industrial action
articles.summary: Nipsa has been holding meetings with members working across the health service and said they had given a clear message over their frustrations.
articles.body:
The public services union, Nipsa, is to ballot healthcare members for industrial action over pay and conditions.

Following a meeting between union leaders and Health Minister Robbie Butler, they said it was "clear that the time for talking is over", with Nipsa assistant secretary Kevin Kelly stating health workers had "reached a tipping point".

The union has been demanding this year's pay award to be implemented immediately, alongside pay reform parity with other regions in the UK and the extension of the Real Living Wage to those in the care sector.

The Department of Health said implementing the 2026-27 pay award and Real Living Wage would cost about £280m.

Nipsa has been holding meetings with members working across the health service and said they had given a clear message over their frustrations.

In its letter to healthcare members, Nipsa said workers should "not have to face increasing workloads, unsafe staffing levels, threat to jobs and continued cuts to vital services".

The union said it was now progressing legal steps to hold the ballot, which will run from 21 October and close next month.

"Our members are telling us they have had enough of being asked to do more with less while services are cut, staff go unrecognised and pay issues remain unresolved," Kelly said.

He added that workers are still waiting for the 2026-27 pay award, with many low-paid staff waiting for the Real Living Wage. He said there remains ongoing frustration around pay reform parity.

"At the same time, the Executive is expecting health and social care organisations to deliver cuts of more than 12% over the next three years. Our members have been crystal clear. Enough is enough," Kelly added.

Last year's pay offer was also delayed, with the Department of Health making the offer in November in order to avoid threatened industrial action.

At that stage, £200m was signed off for the pay deal.

Health pay is a devolved matter in Northern Ireland.

The Department of Health has said that it currently faces a deficit of between £800m to £1bn.

This week, officials told Stormont's health committee that because the NI Executive had still not agreed a budget, they were continuing to base their financial plans on the multi-year budget paper issued in April.

articles.summary: Inmet alerta para baixa umidade em municípios do RN até segunda-feira (12). Umidade pode ficar entre 20% e 30%; veja as cidades e os cuidados.
articles.body:
Beber água pode reduzir os efeitos da baixa umidade do ar — Foto: Imagem ilustrativa

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu um alerta de perigo potencial para baixa umidade do ar em 70 municípios do Rio Grande do Norte. O aviso começou às 10h18 deste domingo (11) e é válido até as 23h59 desta segunda-feira (12).

Segundo o Inmet, a umidade relativa do ar pode variar entre 20% e 30% nas localidades abrangidas pelo alerta. A condição representa baixo risco de incêndios florestais e de problemas à saúde, mas exige cuidados para evitar os efeitos do tempo seco.

O órgão recomenda que a população beba bastante líquido, evite atividades físicas intensas nas horas mais secas e reduza a exposição ao sol nos períodos mais quentes do dia.

Em caso de necessidade, a população pode buscar orientações junto à Defesa Civil, pelo telefone 199, e ao Corpo de Bombeiros, pelo número 193.

articles.title: Samu registra 297 faltas de motoristas em 2026 e tem ambulâncias paradas em Porto Alegre | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa responsável pelo serviço já havia sido multada pela prefeitura, mas recebeu atestado afirmando que cumpria obrigações contratuais.
articles.summary: Empresa responsável pelo serviço já havia sido multada pela prefeitura, mas recebeu atestado afirmando que cumpria obrigações contratuais.
articles.body:
Documentos e planilhas apontam que o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) de Porto Alegre registrou 297 faltas de motoristas neste ano , deixando ambulâncias paradas por ausência de condutores. No mesmo período, também foram contabilizados 106 atrasos de motoristas .

Os problemas, no entanto, já apareciam no ano passado. Em fevereiro, motoristas da empresa Gerir Hospitalar faltaram ao serviço e não foram substituídos dentro do prazo de duas horas estabelecido em contrato. Ao longo daquele mês, nove ambulâncias ficaram paradas por falta de condutor. Reportagem do Fantástico deste domingo (11) detalhou a situação; veja a reportagem acima .

A situação foi informada à empresa e à coordenação do Samu pelo fiscal responsável pelo contrato. Em dezembro, a Prefeitura de Porto Alegre aplicou uma multa de R$ 34.718,34 por descumprimento contratual .

Em nota, a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde (SMS) afirma que "acompanha os apontamentos relacionados ao Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) de Porto Alegre e apura as situações relatadas". Leia a nota completa abaixo .

Atestado foi emitido após aplicação de multa

Apesar da sanção, no mês seguinte uma funcionária do Samu assinou um atestado de capacidade técnica em favor da Gerir Hospitalar .

No documento, consta que os serviços teriam sido prestados com "bom desempenho operacional" e que a empresa havia cumprido fielmente suas obrigações. O texto também afirma que, até aquele momento, não havia fatos que desabonassem a empresa técnica ou comercialmente .

Um ex-funcionário do Samu ouvido pela reportagem questionou a emissão do documento:

"Esse documento é imoral. E não poderia ter tido um documento emitido em favor da empresa por um servidor do SAMU assinado, dizendo que a empresa tem capacidade técnica. Isso não poderia acontecer", diz.

Em março deste ano, o secretário municipal da Saúde, Fernando Ritter, validou a sanção aplicada contra a empresa em dezembro . Questionado posteriormente sobre o atestado, afirmou que o documento seria reavaliado .

"Diante dos fatos, obviamente, que a gente vai reavaliar para a gente não permitir que essa instituição possa participar da licitação. O contrato segue e a gente vai ter reuniões com eles, obviamente, fazer as sanções até entrar a nova instituição que vai assumir esse papel de colocar os condutores dentro do SAMU", afirma.

Ambulância em Porto Alegre — Foto: Reprodução/ RBS TV

Os reflexos da falta de veículos disponíveis foram acompanhados pela reportagem.

Um idoso de 71 anos, que sofre de uma doença degenerativa do sistema nervoso central, aguardava atendimento com fortes dores na barriga. Segundo a mulher que estava com ele, não era possível transportá-lo de carro.

Em outro caso, uma ambulância levou uma hora e meia para chegar a uma ocorrência envolvendo um acidente de trânsito.

A reportagem também foi informada, por um funcionário do Samu, sobre chamados que estavam na fila. Em uma das ocorrências, um motociclista estava com a perna presa em um carro. No local, a reportagem confirmou que o Samu ainda não havia chegado.

Um socorrista, que pediu para não ser identificado por temer represálias, afirmou que a indisponibilidade de uma ambulância pode afetar uma grande área de atendimento .

"Fica em torno de 90 a 100 mil habitantes desassistidos durante esse período", comenta.

Questionado sobre casos de pacientes que aguardavam mais de cinco horas pelo serviço, o secretário municipal da Saúde afirmou que desconhecia a situação.

O mesmo atestado de capacidade técnica emitido pelo Samu foi utilizado pela Gerir Hospitalar para conseguir outro contrato, desta vez com a Prefeitura de Glorinha.

Segundo o prefeito Leonardo Carvalho, a contratação de enfermeiro e técnico de enfermagem foi interrompida depois que o município tomou conhecimento das informações relacionadas ao documento .

"Após as informações que o atestado de capacidade técnica eram inverídicas e isso prejudicava o processo licitatório, a gente suspendeu cautelarmente o contrato por prudência", revela Carvalho.

A reportagem solicitou ao diretor da Gerir Hospitalar um posicionamento sobre o atestado de capacidade técnica, mas não houve retorno.

Sobre as faltas de motoristas, a empresa informou que criou o "prêmio assiduidade", uma gratificação em dinheiro destinada a incentivar o cumprimento das escalas.

A Gerir Hospitalar também afirmou que os condutores precisam ter qualificações específicas e que isso reduz significativamente a quantidade de profissionais disponíveis para substituições imediatas.

O que diz a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde

"A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde (SMS) acompanha os apontamentos relacionados ao Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) de Porto Alegre e apura as situações relatadas.

Em relação aos tempos de atendimento, a média geral é de 26 minutos. Nos casos graves, o tempo médio é de 15 minutos, enquanto nas ocorrências envolvendo pacientes em parada cardíaca é de 12 minutos. A prioridade de cada chamado é definida conforme a gravidade e os protocolos assistenciais. Nos casos relacionados à saúde mental, é necessária a participação de profissionais da segurança pública para garantir a segurança do transporte, portanto, o Samu depende também de efetivo policial disponível para auxiliar nos atendimentos.

Entre julho de 2025 e setembro de 2026, foram registradas 1.507 horas de ausência de profissionais, diante de aproximadamente 245 mil horas de plantão contratadas, o equivalente a cerca de 0,6% da carga horária prevista. A SMS esclarece que a ausência de um profissional na escala não significa, necessariamente, que tenha havido interrupção do atendimento. As horas não cumpridas são glosadas, ou seja, descontadas dos valores pagos à empresa terceirizada. Dessa forma, o valor global do contrato não corresponde ao pagamento integral de horas eventualmente não executadas.

A SMS instaurou processo administrativo sancionatório contra a empresa responsável pelo serviço, que poderá resultar na aplicação de penalidades, incluindo o impedimento de participar de licitações, conforme o enquadramento legal e a conclusão do processo."

articles.title: Confronting the ‘largest energy security threat’
articles.summary: The head of the International Energy Agency, Fatih Birol, discusses the challenges facing the global economy.
articles.body:
The head of the International Energy Agency (IEA) says we are facing the biggest energy crisis ever.

More than seven months on, it continues with little relief in sight. The US-Israel war on Iran is driving the crisis, which has disrupted global shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for 20 percent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas.

That has sent fuel prices soaring, interrupted supply chains and raised fears of a serious energy shortage.

IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol says global oil stocks are declining fast. G7 countries and members of the IEA have tapped into their strategic emergency reserves. But relief has been short-lived and the global economy is still feeling the pain.

The Russia-Ukraine war is putting additional strain on the oil industry, as both countries target each other’s energy facilities.

Birol says if tensions in the Middle East are not resolved, it could have serious consequences for the world economy. He warns of challenging months ahead as winter approaches in the Northern Hemisphere.

Birol says it will take time for the energy sector to recover from this crisis, and he acknowledges the industry will likely never be the same again.

articles.title: Arcebispo de Aparecida pede paz desarmada e critica ódio em homilia | G1
articles.standfirst: Celebração das 9h é a principal da Festa da Padroeira e marcou a primeira participação de Dom Mário Antônio da Silva como arcebispo na data; homilias anteriores também abordaram temas sociais e políticos.
articles.summary: O arcebispo de Aparecida, Dom Mário Antônio da Silva, defendeu uma paz desarmada e criticou o ódio político durante a missa solene da Festa da Padroeira.
articles.body:
O arcebispo de Aparecida , Dom Mário Antônio Silva, defendeu nesta segunda-feira (12), dia da Padroeira, uma "paz desarmada e desarmante" e afirmou que o Evangelho não autoriza os cristãos a odiar quem pensa diferente. Durante a homilia, ele criticou divisões, preconceitos e confrontos, e disse que a missão dos fiéis é construir pontes "onde alguém abre precipícios" e promover a reconciliação.

Ao falar durante a homilia sobre a necessidade de construir uma “paz desarmada e desarmante”, dom Mário Antônio da Silva fez referência ao papa Leão XIV, que tem defendido essa mensagem. O arcebispo criticou a lógica dos conflitos e das divisões e afirmou que os ensinamentos de Jesus não justificam o ódio contra quem pensa diferente

“Sabemos que Jesus manda construir a paz. E aqui, escutando Leão XIV, uma paz desarmada e desarmante. Mas muitas vezes alimentamos divisões. Falamos com armamentos, com guerras e tantos confrontos entre nós. O Evangelho, queridos irmãos e irmãs, não nos autoriza a odiar quem pensa diferente e nem a matar os inimigos”, afirmou.

Na sequência, dom Mário afirmou que a mensagem cristã incentiva o diálogo e a aproximação entre as pessoas.

“O Evangelho, sim, nos autoriza a construir pontes onde alguém abre precipícios ou túneis, onde alguém ergue muros”, declarou.

Ao longo da homilia, dom Mário Antônio da Silva fez um apelo contra a indiferença diante do sofrimento humano e das injustiças. Ele citou crianças feridas, idosos abandonados, guerras e a destruição da natureza entre os problemas que afetam a população do Brasil e do mundo.

“Quem escuta Deus não pode ficar indiferente diante da fome, da pobreza, da violência, da solidão. Não pode ficar indiferente diante das famílias feridas, das crianças também feridas, dos jovens sem esperança, dos idosos abandonados. Não podemos ficar indiferentes diante das guerras, da destruição da natureza e de tantos outros males que nos afetam, que afetam a população do Brasil e do mundo”, afirmou.

Dom Mário Antonio da Silva celebra a missa solene de 12 de outubro na basílica em Aparecida — Foto: Reprodução;/TV Aparecida

Apesar das referências e o tom político, dom Mário Antônio da Silva não fez menções diretas às eleições nem à polêmica envolvendo a imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida e os nomes do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidatos ao 2º turno - saiba mais sobre o caso clicando aqui.

A missa deste ano marca uma mudança na condução das celebrações após a saída de Dom Orlando Brandes , que esteve à frente da Arquidiocese de Aparecida por nove anos. O pedido de renúncia do religioso foi aceito pelo papa após ele completar 80 anos. Dom Mário tomou posse como novo arcebispo em 2 de maio de 2026.

A homilia de dom Mário Antônio seguiu uma linha semelhante à adotada por seu antecessor, pois Dom Orlando Brandes também costumava abordar questões sociais em suas mensagens na Festa da Padroeira. Em anos anteriores, o então arcebispo de Aparecida tratou de temas como desigualdade social, preservação ambiental, racismo, aborto e o papel dos representantes eleitos, com apelos à justiça e à atenção aos mais pobres - relembre no fim da reportagem.

Dom Mário Antônio da Silva e dom Orlando Brandes, em missa solene na Basílica de Aparecida. — Foto: Reprodução/A12

Considerada a principal celebração da Festa da Padroeira, a missa solene das 9h desta segunda reuniu milhares de fiéis e autoridades no Santuário Nacional, em Aparecida (SP). Essa foi a primeira vez de Dom Mário Antônio à frente das comemorações de 12 de outubro no cargo, após a aposentadoria de Dom Orlando Brandes.

Entre as autoridades presentes estavam o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), a deputada federal Tabata Amaral (PSB-SP), o político João Campos (PSB), e o presidente nacional do PSD, Gilberto Kassab. Também participou da celebração o ministro da Saúde, Alexandre Padilha. A cerimônia reuniu ainda o prefeito de Aparecida e representantes da Polícia Militar e do Corpo de Bombeiros.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que disputam o segundo turno da eleição presidencial, não participam da celebração em Aparecida. Os dois têm compromissos religiosos previstos em Brasília nesta segunda-feira.

A Basílica de Aparecida estava lotada para a celebração da missa das 9h. — Foto: Lucas Tavares/g1

Ao longo dos últimos anos, as homilias da missa solene de 12 de outubro ganharam repercussão também por abordarem questões sociais e temas presentes no debate político nacional.

Em 2022, durante a reta final das eleições presidenciais, dom Orlando Brandes fez críticas ao ódio e à mentira. Na ocasião, afirmou que era preciso vencer os “dragões do ódio e da mentira” e falou sobre desemprego, fome e participação dos eleitores.

Em 2023, o arcebispo abordou temas como aborto , preservação ambiental, justiça e direitos humanos. Durante a homilia, defendeu a proteção da vida e criticou o desmatamento. Na ocasião, também relacionou suas declarações sobre o aborto ao debate em curso no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

A celebração deste ano ocorre em meio à disputa eleitoral e à repercussão de conteúdos falsos envolvendo Nossa Senhora Aparecida. A homilia de dom Mário é um dos momentos centrais da missa e deve concentrar a atenção dos fiéis, das autoridades e dos jornalistas presentes.

O dia 12 de outubro reúne milhares de romeiros no Santuário Nacional para homenagear Nossa Senhora Aparecida, Padroeira do Brasil. A programação inclui sete missas ao longo do dia, consagração solene na Basílica Histórica e uma procissão no início da noite.

Por volta das 8h40, o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin e outros políticos já estavam na Basílica de Aparecida, à espera do início da missa solene das 9h, que será presidida pelo arcebispo de Aparecida, dom Mário Antônio da Silva. — Foto: Marcelo Sarlo/g1

articles.title: Ex-tabelião é condenado por falsificar certidões e desviar dinheiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Esquema envolveu a regularização de apartamentos na Zona Sul de Natal. Ex-tabelião recebeu valor para custos cartoriais, mas não regularizou documentação e entregou certidões falsas.
articles.summary: Esquema envolveu a regularização de apartamentos na Zona Sul de Natal. Ele recebeu valor para custos cartoriais, mas não regularizou documentação e entregou certidões falsas.
articles.body:
Imagem ilustrativa de escrituras de imóveis — Foto: Sérgio Willian/Divulgação/ARQUIVO

Um ex-tabelião do Cartório de Montanhas , no Rio Grande do Norte, foi condenado a 7 anos e 7 meses de prisão no regime semiaberto por falsificar certidões de imóveis e desviar o dinheiro que era repassado a ele para os custos cartoriais. O nome dele não foi divulgado.

De acordo com o Ministério Público do Rio Grande do Norte, que ofereceu a denúncia na Justiça, a maioria das vítimas do ex-tabelião era investidores espanhóis.

O esquema ocorreu entre os anos de 2009 e 2012 e envolveu a regularização de apartamentos na Zona Sul de Natal . Segundo o MP, ele se apropriou de R$ 63,8 mil.

O ex-tabelião foi condenado pelos crimes de peculato e falsificação de documento público. Ele também vai ter que pagar multa, que não teve o valor revelado.

➡️ Segundo o MP, o ex-tabelião já tinha outras condenações, por crimes análogos, que atualmente estão em execução penal e somam um total de 16 anos, 4 meses e 20 dias de pena.

Entenda como funcionava o golpe, segundo o MP

Segundo o MP, os investidores compraram imóveis na Zona Sul de Natal e contrataram os serviços do ex-tabelião para lavrar as escrituras e fazer os registros em cartório.

O processo judicial aponta que o ex-tabelião teria recebido pagamentos para cobrir as taxas do cartório e os impostos de transmissão das propriedades.

No entanto, ele não efetuou os registros no 7º Ofício de Notas de Natal, responsável pela região dos imóveis.

Para enganar os compradores e a imobiliária intermediadora, o homem entregou 12 certidões falsificadas que simulavam a conclusão do processo registral.

"Na sentença foram destacadas as provas que confirmam que o ex-tabelião recebia o dinheiro aproveitando-se do cargo que ocupava e não dava destino legal aos recursos", informou o MPRN.

A Justiça do Rio Grande do Norte aplicou contra o suspeito o cometimento do crime de peculato-apropriação porque cartórios funcionam por delegação do Poder Público.

Dessa forma, quem atua como tabelião é considerado funcionário público para fins penais.

Como o recebimento do dinheiro das taxas e impostos foi realizado na condição de tabelião e não foi dado o destino exigido por lei, a conduta é enquadrada em um crime mais grave contra a administração pública.

articles.title: Gaza: Still Reporting
articles.summary: When Israel orders an evacuation of Gaza City, a journalist documents the displacement while living it with her family.
articles.body:
Maram Humaid spends her days reporting, writing and listening to the stories of Palestinians living through Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. When Israel orders the total clearance of Gaza City for the first time during the war, Maram goes through one of the most difficult periods of her life.

As she navigates motherhood, food scarcity and the deaths of colleagues, Maram continues documenting the war around her, aware of the risks that come with her work. Alongside her family, Maram moves through a city being evacuated. She meets Palestinians who have made the painful decision to leave and those who have made the impossible choice to stay.

Gaza: Still Reporting is a documentary film by Mohammed Sawwaf, Salah Al-Haw and Ibrahim Al-Otla.

articles.title: Enchente deixa mais de 100 estrangeiros ilhados no Nepal. | G1
articles.standfirst: Cheia de rio destruiu trilhas e pontes na região central do país. Equipes de busca já resgataram 96 pessoas, mas cinco moradores continuam desaparecidos.
articles.summary: Cheia de rio destruiu trilhas e pontes na região central do país. Equipes de busca já resgataram 96 pessoas, mas cinco moradores continuam desaparecidos.
articles.body:
Imagem de drone mostra as áreas afetadas pela cheia do rio Budhi Gandaki após um deslizamento de terra a seco no vilarejo de Chumnubri, distrito de Gorkha, no Nepal. — Foto: Reuters / National Trust for Nature Conservation-Manaslu Conservation Area Project

Mais de 100 estrangeiros que andavam por trilhas estão ilhados em diferentes locais após a cheia de um rio na região central do Nepal no fim de semana arrastar trilhas e pontes, disse uma autoridade nesta segunda-feira.

As autoridades resgataram 96 pessoas, incluindo nove estrangeiros, depois que um deslizamento de terra no domingo no distrito de Gorkha, a cerca de 100 km a oeste de Katmandu, bloqueou o rio Budhi Gandaki, causando inundações rio abaixo.

O rio é um afluente do rio Trishuli, localizado rio abaixo de outro afluente, onde o colapso de uma geleira causou uma enchente catastrófica em agosto, que matou 1.457 pessoas, com milhares ainda desaparecidas.

O exército afirmou que a mais recente operação de resgate continuava nesta segunda-feira, mesmo com o recuo das águas.

Não houve relatos de mortes, mas cinco moradores de vilarejos locais estão incomunicáveis após a cheia do rio, que carregava uma lama preta e destroços, arrastar casas e danificar infraestruturas, incluindo três usinas hidrelétricas, segundo autoridades nacionais de desastres.

Bhuwan Raj Ojha, uma autoridade do Projeto da Área de Conservação de Manaslu (MACP, na sigla em inglês), que inclui uma rota popular de trilhas, disse que havia mais de 100 trilheiros estrangeiros ilhados em diferentes áreas que não conseguiam retornar porque parte do caminho havia sido levada pelas águas.

"Os trilheiros que desejam retornar por causa da enchente precisam ser resgatados. Aqueles que querem continuar a trilha podem fazê-lo a partir de locais seguros", disse Ojha à Reuters a partir de Gorkha.

"Existem restaurantes e casas de chá ao longo da rota. Eles estão em segurança."

O Centro Internacional para o Desenvolvimento Integrado de Montanhas (ICIMOD) informou que a enchente mais recente pode ter sido desencadeada pelo rompimento de um bloqueio temporário do rio criado por um deslizamento de terra, de acordo com relatos preliminares de autoridades nepalesas analisados pelo órgão.

"Este evento é mais um lembrete de quão expostas as comunidades nas montanhas e os corredores de rios continuam a perigos repentinos e em cascata", disse Pema Gyamtsho, diretor-geral do ICIMOD.

"Embora os esforços de resposta devam continuar sendo a prioridade imediata, entender o que causou essa enchente será fundamental para reduzir riscos futuros e fortalecer a resiliência."

articles.title: Days before her wedding, engineering student found dead in Maharashtra gorge, boyfriend held
articles.summary: KOLHAPUR: A 25-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murdering his 23-year-old girlfriend, an engineering student whose body was found nearly
articles.body: KOLHAPUR: A 25-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murdering his 23-year-old girlfriend, an engineering student whose body was found nearly 1,000ft below a cliff at Naikwadi waterfalls Maharashtra's Kolhapur.Police came to know of the death Saturday when Sripad Vadar walked into a PS and reported that Tarrannum Naik, a third-year student who lived with her maternal grandmother in Gargoti, had fallen into a gorge from a cliff.Police sent a team to the remote site and retrieved her body."He told us they had been in a relationship for five-and-a-half years and were distressed because her family had fixed her marriage elsewhere. According to him, the couple had decided to die by suicide together. He claimed she jumped into the gorge, but he lost his nerve at the last moment," sub-divisional police officer Vivek Patil said.Naikwadi waterfalls are deep inside forested terrain, about 50km from Gargoti. The falls were dry after the monsoon, and no visitors were in the area when the couple reached the spot Friday, police said.Police registered a case under section 140(3) of BNS, relating to wrongful confinement. But examination of messages exchanged between the couple raised doubts about Sripad's account."The chat history does not support the account he gave us about a suicide pact. The messages suggested Sripad was upset over Tarrannum's family's decision to get her married to someone else. That raised serious doubts and led us to invoke BNS section 103(1) for murder," Patil said.Accused Sripad, also from Gargoti, worked with his brother, a local contractor. On Sunday, a court remanded Sripad in police custody for five days.Police have seized mobile phones of both Tarrannum and the accused for forensic analysis. Police are awaiting the autopsy report.Tarrannum's last rites were performed at her native Patgaon. Her marriage had been fixed for Nov 12. articles.title: Why Halloween is now bigger than Christmas for some attractions
articles.summary: From scare parks to pumpkin patches, Halloween is driving huge crowds and spending.
articles.body:
Halloween has become so popular that some attractions now make more money from the spooky season than Christmas, operators say.

From pumpkin festivals and haunted mazes to zombie experiences, businesses say demand for Halloween events has soared as the celebration grows from a single night into a month-long attraction.

At Avon Valley Adventure Park near Bath, Halloween activities now generate around a third of the site's annual income. Founder Doug Douglas said: "Halloween is really important for us, it has surpassed Christmas."

"We make half of our turnover in October, and one third comes from the week of Halloween alone," said David Gaze, owner at Chaplins fancy dress shop in Bristol.

Retailers, farm attractions and scare parks say people are spending more on costumes, decorations and immersive experiences, helping to make October one of their busiest times of the year.

Chaplins has been a staple in the city centre for 35 years, back when people wore fancy dress on New Year's Eve.

"People don't do that so much anymore, now it's mostly for Halloween," Gaze said.

Last year, it saw its busiest October to date, with customers individually spending an average of £40 on fancy costumes and accessories.

"People are spending more and the week of Halloween is our busiest every year, we get queues outside the front door."

"It's usually what people are seeing on TV that sells well. Some years ago it was boiler suits from Squid Game, everyone wanted that," he added.

Halloween's growing popularity is also benefiting supermarkets and retailers selling sweets, decorations and party supplies.

In a survey carried out in March by market researcher IGD , 36% of shoppers said they planned to celebrate Halloween this year, up from 27% in 2025.

Harvir Dhillon, lead economist at the British Retail Consortium, said at this time of year "retailers will be competing hard" as they see "greater demand for sweets and chocolate, as well as decorations and costumes".

"Halloween has become an increasingly popular occasion for people to enjoy," he said.

And some like to start celebrations as early as possible, like Catarina Vieira, who lives in Swindon and started decorating her house last week.

"I spend between £150 to £200 every year on Halloween," she said, adding that is mostly on decorations and thrill events.

Vieira said feeling scared about monsters is a "fun escape" from the stresses of her everyday life as an A&E doctor.

"I think having a holiday where you are scared about something that is 'real', instead of the usual daily mental pressures, touches me in a way."

"It helps me escape reality for a bit, being scared about something that is tangibly scary, like monsters or bats," she added.

But it is not just retail. Many farmers have found ways to diversify their land, by turning it into lucrative family attractions on Halloween.

In October, pumpkin patches where you can pick your own pumpkin are high in demand, with popularity being largely driven by social media .

Farms often charge an entry fee which can vary significantly, from around £2 to £15 per person, for children and adults alike.

With the biggest whoppers selling for upwards of £15 a piece, a fun family day out pushing wheelbarrows full of pumpkins can become costly, yet some attractions sell out quickly.

Heather Parry, managing agent at National Farm Attractions Network (NFAN), said Halloween has become one of the biggest seasons of the year for some farmers.

"Ten years ago, a pumpkin patch was a field and a wheelbarrow. Now it's a wonderful experience for the whole family," she said.

The network has around 200 members and "almost all" embrace the spooky season with a mix of "maize mazes, after-dark trails, scare attractions and pumpkin festivals".

"Diversification is key for many farms to thrive," she added, saying it has helped them mitigate existing challenges.

Parry said: "Farmers are coping with climate change, change in government support and requirements, high input costs, the changes to inheritance tax relief on farms along with many other things."

"Halloween gives farms a short, high-footfall season," she added.

Doug Douglas, founder of Avon Valley Adventure Park, said their Halloween events grow every year and now generate a third of their yearly income.

"We turn over £2m from our activities in October," said Douglas.

He added: "Halloween is really important for us, it has surpassed Christmas."

The park sits on a 90-acre farm in Keynsham, near Bath, and was once a fruit farm after his dad bought the land more than 30 years ago.

Now Douglas runs family activities during school holidays and seasonal events, including for Halloween and Christmas.

FEAR Scream Park is their award-winning attraction offering "immersive scare experiences" over 13 nights in October, with scare mazes and live actors.

This month, they are expecting around 30,000 visitors but Douglas said the event is not "massively profitable" due to costs.

"It costs us about £750,000 to put on the event," he said. "On staff wages alone, we employ about 200 staff, including around 120 actors."

In addition, they run a popular pumpkin event which attracts around 120,000 people each year.

Douglas said: "Everyone thinks they're easy [to put on], but we've got fire shows, stilt walkers, actors, we put in a big bar and we turn it into a real festival field."

At HMP Gloucester, it is zombies that visitors must try and escape from as they walk past old prison cells, facing all sorts of scary encounters.

The post-apocalyptic zombie experience 'Salvation-Z' is run by Gloucester Prison Events at the defunct prison and employs around 30 actors from the local area, according to actor manager Clive Barzillia.

"We get lots and lots of people apply for the acting roles. They have to audition and if they're shy we have to shake it out of them," he said.

He said actors are taught welfare training and paramedics are also on site.

"Ultimately it's a safe environment", he said.

"Actors are trained to look out for people that might be vulnerable or sensitive, and they can adapt their acting."

He added: "People get right into the spirit of it," talking about the visitors.

"We've noticed they want to come in fancy dress now, they want to become characters themselves."

articles.title: If Netanyahu goes, does anything really change for Palestinians?
articles.summary: Analysts say opposition win in polls may bring only marginal change and no fundamental shift on Gaza, West Bank.
articles.body:
Four rival Israeli political movements have agreed to work together in a bid to unseat Israel’s longest serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

The factions – the Yashar party, the Democrats, the Yisrael Beytenu party and the Together alliance – span different parts of Israel’s political spectrum but say they are united in their goal to “preserve and strengthen Israel as a Jewish and democratic state”.

The opposition grouping is in a close battle with a pro-Netanyahu coalition heading into the October 27 elections , recent polling indicated, although neither side appeared on track to win a parliamentary majority.

The election comes as Israel faces a series of domestic crises that are tearing at its social fabric, including questions over political accountability for alleged corruption and security failures , disputes over ultra-Orthodox military service and efforts to exclude Arab parties from political life . The country also faces growing backlash abroad , including from allies, over its continuing attacks on Gaza and Lebanon as well as settlements, which are illegal under international law, and settler pogroms in the occupied West Bank.

Analysts said the combination makes the upcoming elections among the most consequential in Israel’s history but even an opposition victory may bring only marginal change for Palestinians suffering record levels of settler violence and mass displacement. While the opposition alliance has taken Netanyahu to task personally, there is little daylight between them when it comes to Israel’s foundational policies in Gaza and the West Bank.

“Palestinians should not expect a fundamental change in Israeli policy if the Netanyahu bloc loses power,” said analyst Samer Jaber, a doctoral researcher specialising in political economy at Royal Holloway, University of London.

“The major political blocs share core positions on the Palestinian question, including support for the existing settlement structure, while the state institutions that formulate and implement policy would remain unchanged,” he added.

The leaders of the four major Jewish-led opposition movements gathered on September 26 and signed a declaration promising not to attack each other in the run-up to the elections and to collaborate in forming a government after the vote.

In addition to Yair Lapid, who leads the official opposition in Israel’s Knesset, the meeting included Gadi Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party; Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together alliance , cofounded by Lapid; Avigdor Lieberman, who heads Yisrael Beiteinu; and Yair Golan, who leads the Democrats. The declaration does not set out an official leader although Eisenkot is viewed as the opposition’s most likely candidate for prime minister. In a joint statement, the figures said defeating the current government was their “shared highest objective”.

Of the four opposition parties, Yashar is projected to be the strongest. A recent poll by Israel’s Channel 12 suggested Yashar would win 23 seats in parliament, the most of any party and more than the 21 seats projected for Netanyahu’s Likud.

Trailing is the Together alliance, projected to win 13 seats, followed by Yisrael Beiteinu and the Democrats, each projected to win nine.

That would give the opposition a combined 54 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, seven short of a majority. Netanyahu’s alliance, which includes several ultra-Orthodox and far-right parties, is projected to win 49 seats.

Arab-led parties, representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population, are projected to win 13 seats, but most leaders of the Jewish-led opposition bloc have ruled out joining forces with them.

Roi Zur, an assistant professor at the University of Essex who leads a research project on Israeli parties’ political ideology and policy, said the anti-Netanyahu coalition has a chance to win if turnout is on its side, noting that several parties that do not “strictly oppose” the prime minister could fall below the 3.25 percent threshold to enter the Knesset, shaking up the balance.

“If these parties waste enough right-wing votes, the opposition might translate their support into power,” Zur told Al Jazeera. “But this might not be enough.”

Even if the opposition alliance manages to find a way to oust Netanyahu, it would likely be weak and incapable – or unwilling – to overhaul Israeli policy in the West Bank and Gaza, analysts said.

“An anti-Netanyahu government will most likely be a very disparate coalition with a very thin majority, if any, in the Knesset. That would make it difficult for such a government to agree on any substantial perceived concessions, such as withdrawing completely from Gaza,” Anders Persson, a political scientist specialising in the Israel-Palestine conflict , told Al Jazeera.

“It would also make it difficult for the international community to meaningfully pressure such a government because there will always be a fear that an anti-Netanyahu government could quickly collapse.”

While their positions vary, most leaders of the anti-Netanyahu alliance have taken hardline positions on Gaza and the West Bank that give Palestinians little reason for optimism.

Yashar’s Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, has called the idea of a Palestinian state “delusional”, and he supports “strengthening” Israeli settlements. However, he opposes full Israeli annexation of the West Bank and has said he would dismantle smaller Israeli outposts not approved by the Israeli government. He also opposes the current government’s E1 settlement plan, which in effect would cut the West Bank in two. On Gaza, Eisenkot supports pursuing a United States-backed peace plan but only from a place of “strength” and only after “Hamas’s total disarmament”.

Israeli attacks across Gaza since the start of a “ceasefire” in October last year have killed nearly 1,500 Palestinians, bringing the overall death toll since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023 to more than 74,000, according to the enclave’s health officials.

Bennett, a former Likud member who served in multiple Netanyahu-led governments, has described himself as “more right-wing” than Netanyahu and advocated exceptionally draconian policies in Gaza, including once calling for a “shoot-to-kill” policy against Palestinians trying to cross into Israel. Bennett staunchly opposes a Palestinian state and supports settlement expansion although he has criticised Israeli settler pogroms against Palestinians. With respect to the future of Gaza, he wants Israeli forces to stay in the enclave until Hamas is disarmed and proposes that Egypt, rather than Turkiye or Qatar, should play a future security role.

Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu party also supports settlement expansion, including the E1 plan. He backs annexing all of Area C of the West Bank – which constitutes 60 percent of the territory and is already under full Israeli control – while transferring control of other parts of the territory to Jordan. On Gaza, his party wants Israel to retain “freedom of action”, cut off water and electricity and eventually transfer governance to “an agreed-upon international entity”.

Golan’s Democrats party is the only one to support a form of two-state solution although it frames it as “responsible separation” that includes the “full demilitarisation” of the Palestinian state and complete Israeli security control of the Jordan Valley and other key areas. His party also supports complete demilitarisation for Gaza and a reconstruction process that involves regional states.

Palestinian lawyer and analyst Diana Buttu said each of the opposition leaders “has supported Israel’s genocide in Gaza” while backing settlements or not believing in full “equality for Palestinians”.

This orientation reflects hardening views within Israeli society itself.

According to a September Pew Research Center poll, only 17 percent of Israeli respondents said peaceful coexistence alongside an independent Palestinian state is possible. And according to an August survey by the Jewish People Policy Institute, 38 percent of Jewish Israeli participants favoured annexing the entire West Bank and more than half supported retaining the settlements as part of any future agreement on a Palestinian state.

Nevertheless, some analysts said a new government could roll back or slow down some of the most “controversial and radical steps” of Israel’s current government, which includes far-right settlement proponents Itamar Ben-Gvir, the minister of national security, and Bezalel Smotrich, the minister of finance. Smotrich last month said Israel should “go to war” in the West Bank and repeat what it “did in Gaza”.

Changes enacted by a new government would likely include suspending the E1 settlement project and cracking down “on extremist settler violence/terrorism in the West Bank”, said Dov Waxman, a professor of political science at the University of California, Los Angeles, who specialises in Israeli politics and the Israel-Palestine conflict.

A new government would also be expected to “allow more humanitarian aid to enter Gaza in a more predictable, consistent manner and for reconstruction to finally begin there”, he added.

Ehab Jabareen, a Palestinian political analyst and researcher in Israel, told Al Jazeera that a new government led by Netanyahu’s opponents would likely be “more receptive to US and international pressure”, giving more space for potential reconstruction in Gaza.

But overall, Jabareen said, such a government is unlikely to alter Israel’s overarching “paradigm” towards Palestinians. “I would expect the difference to be less about whether Israel maintains control over the Palestinians and more about how the control is exercised, legitimised and managed,” he said.

Amjad Iraqi, senior analyst for Israel and Palestine at the International Crisis Group, said any “shades of difference” would be meaningful for Palestinians who are currently “suffering nearly uninhibited brutality”.

“We’re at a point of mitigation,” Iraqi told Al Jazeera. “It is about trying to lessen the harms. Palestinians are not in a position to expect any kind of radical shift, but every life saved, every piece of land saved matters a lot for people on the ground.”

articles.title: Swansea's Makenzy Beard features in Portrait Artist of the Year
articles.summary: Makenzy Beard discovered her talent after she decided to try out her mother's old paint brushes.
articles.body:
A 19-year-old painter from Swansea who has sold artwork for tens of thousands of pounds is due to appear on the TV art competition, Portrait Artist of the Year.

Makenzy Beard discovered her talent for painting during the Covid lockdown after she decided to try out her mother's old paint brushes in the garden shed .

She said she felt "up for the challenge" of painting celebrity sitters in front of TV cameras and a highly respected panel of judges.

Beard is currently putting together her second collection of work, which will include about 20 paintings that reflect her "view of the world" and interest in philosophy.

After completing several portraits against the clock, the winner of the competition on SkyArts gets a £10,000 commission to paint British actor and musician Damian Lewis for the National Portrait Gallery.

"I suppose I wanted to give it a go. I've watched the show and it seemed like a challenge, so I thought why not," Beard said.

Since displaying one of her first portraits at the Royal Academy Summer Show in 2021, she has sold paintings for thousands of pounds and raised more than £45,000 for charitable causes.

"I don't think I had time to reflect much on what I thought of the work because I was having a lot of opinions from other people.

"As I've got older, people still, I suppose, have some nice things [to say] about my work, because it's not about my age but the work itself."

Beard said her latest works have more depth, especially since developing a keen interest in philosophy.

She said: "I think having not been taught, everything I do is quite intuitive. I just do what I feel like and that's always changing.

"This collection tries to capture things I see in the world and [they] have little messages."

Entering the art world at a young age has been a "crazy" experience, which she said she had found "difficult to understand", especially with some of her pieces selling for tens of thousands of pounds.

"It's difficult to navigate because unlike lots of things where you work hard and kind of get results and do well, with art it's so subjective," she said.

"You can work hard and absolutely love something and if someone else doesn't, it doesn't mean it doesn't have value."

Beard's latest collection covers a variety of topics including animal cruelty, child poverty and mental health.

There are also some "light hearted" takes on some of life's challenges.

"I do see the potential for my work to become more political as I get older but I have no desire to force my work into a direction.

"If things come to me and I want it to come through in my art then it will, but I don't have a headstrong vision in terms of political stuff.

"I still feel a little bit young, too naive to project any of my opinions on these things."

Beard said she's looking to partner with a gallery in order to display her latest collection.

articles.title: Yorkshire Wildlife Park tiger attack prompts health and safety inquiry
articles.summary: Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains shut after a man was fatally attacked by a tiger on Saturday.
articles.body:
A health and safety investigation has been launched into the death of a man who was killed by a tiger after he entered its enclosure.

Yorkshire Wildlife Park was closed over the weekend following reports of a man climbing down into the enclosure from a walkway on Saturday afternoon.

An eyewitness described seeing the man wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in and was attacked. South Yorkshire Police confirmed he was visiting the park on his own.

"I can confirm that, in line with our statutory duties, the council has launched a health and safety investigation," a City of Doncaster Council spokesperson said.

Dan Swaine, the local authority's executive director of place, said the council was "deeply saddened" by the incident and sent its "deepest sympathies" to the man's family and those who were at the scene.

"We are also working with multiple agencies, including the police and health agencies, and are supporting the Yorkshire Wildlife Park in response to the incident," he said.

"At this time, we won't be commenting further on the individual or the investigation and we ask that the privacy of those involved is respected at this difficult time."

The wildlife park remains closed for third day as investigations continue.

A park spokesperson said: "Due to the events over the weekend, the park will remain closed today. Thank you for your understanding."

South Yorkshire Police said the man died at the scene and his family were being supported by officers. "Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time," the force said.

Yorkshire Wildlife Park said the rare Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.

Cars could be seen coming and going from the park earlier, but there were no visitors.

In a message to ticket holders on Monday morning, Yorkshire Wildlife Park said anyone with a booking would be contacted within the next five days to reschedule.

Angela Seivewright, 47, from Bawtry, was laying flowers outside the park gates in tribute to the deceased man. She said she had an annual pass and had visited many times with her two children.

"My daughter was unfortunately sent the video and she's a teenager," she said.

"I found it very distressing, but I think what I've found more distressing is the reaction of the public that I received when I said I hope the human is OK.

"I was surprised at the amount of anger and hatred the people seemed to have towards the gentleman."

On Saturday evening, police said they were aware of videos circulating online and encouraged people not to share the footage.

Dr Campbell Murn, a previous member of the government's zoo expert committee and lecturer at the University of Reading, said while it was a tragic incident, determined people could get inside zoo enclosures.

"I view it in the same way a determined thief will get into somebody's house or somebody's car and despite the best security systems and enclosures sometimes these things happen," he said.

"One of the fundamental approaches of a modern zoo is to give people a wildlife experience and keep them safe so they can learn and they can enjoy being near the animals, but keeping a safety distance that is relevant but not making it too heavy handed."

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Murn said public safety was an "enormous consideration" for zoo standards in the UK.

A spokesperson for the Born Free Foundation, which campaigns to phase out zoos, called for an "urgent review" into "how the man managed to enter the enclosure and what happened next".

Born Free's co-founder Will Travers said: "Putting dangerous wild animals on public display in zoos and safari parks creates a false relationship with humans.

"Visitors are encouraged to get up close and personal - that is a deeply unnatural situation and not without risk."

Jo Judge, chief executive of the British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums, said zoos were subject to a "huge number" of risk assessments, along with full inspections every six years and periodic inspections every three.

"There are so many processes and procedures in place to ensure the safety of everybody who is visiting zoos and aquariums and these are incredibly rare incidents," she said.

"Zoos are actually one of the safest places you can visit."

She added the body had received many messages of support for the Yorkshire Wildlife Park.

"There's no concern from the rest of the community, because we know how well regulated we are, how well licensed we are, all of the procedures and policies that have to be put in place to make sure zoos and aquariums are safe for staff, for the animals and for the public."

The tiger has been at Yorkshire Wildlife Park since it was moved from Dyreparken in Norway in February 2025 as part of the international EAZA European Endangered Species Programme for Amur tigers.

Dyreparken biologist Helene Axelsen said Altai was born at the site in 2021.

She said: "We were deeply saddened to hear about the tragic incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park over the weekend.

"Our thoughts are first and foremost with the victim's family, loved ones, and the entire team at Yorkshire Wildlife Park during this extremely difficult time."

Retired animal behaviourist Dr David Sands said anyone entering an enclosure would be seen as a threat.

"The animal is just being the animal that one million years of evolution has produced," he said.

"It's the top apex predator of its group of animals and I don't think any blame can be put on to the animal itself.

"Could you make the enclosure higher, bigger, more inner protections - well, where do you stop?"

articles.title: What do emergency and governor rule in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa mean?
articles.summary: Pakistan has taken control of a province governed by Imran Khan’s PTI. Here’s what the move means and what happens next.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan – The federal government has taken direct control of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), the northwestern province governed by jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party until now.

President Asif Ali Zardari signed a proclamation on Sunday, on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, imposing a state of emergency and declaring that the provincial government could no longer function in accordance with the Constitution, the legal basis for governor’s rule. On Monday, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the province’s chief minister, Sohail Afridi, was detained.

“The fundamental grounds for imposition of emergency are law and order, fight against terrorism, and to save innocent people from the dreadful consequences of terrorist activities,” Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said at a news conference in Islamabad on Sunday, alongside Information Minister Ataullah Tarar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and other officials.

PTI, which has governed the province since 2013, has rejected the move. It came after talks collapsed between the federal government and the PTI over a planned march to Islamabad demanding the party leader’s release.

Here is what the two measures mean, who now runs the province and how long the arrangement could last.

Under the government’s decision, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi will take over the functions of the provincial government. Kundi belongs to the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), an ally of Sharif’s government.

Parliament — where Sharif’s Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz), the PPP and their other allies hold a majority — takes over the powers of the provincial assembly, where PTI has a majority. The chief minister, ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general “shall forthwith cease to hold office”, the proclamation says.

Hassan Abdullah Niazi, a Lahore-based lawyer and adjunct faculty member at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), offered a different interpretation.

“However, this does not mean that the KP Assembly or its elected chief minister have been permanently removed. It is more akin to thinking they are dysfunctional until the emergency is lifted, at which point they must be restored,” he told Al Jazeera.

An 11-member advisory council will assist Kundi. The army, already deployed in the province, is expected to assist him and his team in maintaining law and order.

A separate federal order has established a secretariat for 12 “designated districts”, most of them in the former tribal areas along the Afghan border. It will be headed by an additional chief secretary, whose orders will carry the same legal effect as those of the provincial government.

“No province has been divided anywhere. It is only that these are the war-hit districts where more funding and more focus will be needed at this time, and for that this has been set apart,” Naqvi said at Sunday’s news conference.

The order also states that the constitutional provision requiring the judiciary to be separated from the executive “shall not apply” to the designated districts.

“The constitutional provision that mandates the separation of the judiciary from the executive has been suspended, allowing executive officers to perform judicial functions,” Rida Hosain, a Lahore-based constitutional lawyer, told Al Jazeera.

Why did the government invoke both measures?

Article 232 of Pakistan’s Constitution allows the president to declare an emergency when security is threatened by an “internal disturbance beyond the power of a provincial government to control”.

Article 234 applies when a governor reports that a province cannot be governed in accordance with the Constitution.

The proclamation cites “terrorist” attacks of “unprecedented level of violent intensity” and says the provincial government “has failed to demonstrate the ownership, will and intent to adequately deal with the menace of terrorism”.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank, armed men carried out at least 1,066 attacks in the country in 2025, up from 908 in 2024.

The number rose sharply in 2026 as PICSS recorded 1,232 attacks nationwide in the first nine months – the majority of which occurred in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan province in the southwest.

“But this situation was so grave and exceptional that the requirements in both provisions, the conditions that demand them, were such that both provisions were exercised,” Tarar said.

Information Minister Ataullah Tarar went further, accusing the provincial government of links to armed groups.

“This was the carefully considered view, from start to finish, of all cabinet members that the PTI government in KP is hand in glove with the terrorists,” he said, without providing evidence.

Naqvi said the government had dozens of pieces of evidence against the provincial government. None has been made public.

PTI chairman Gohar Ali Khan questioned why the measures were applied across the province if the security concerns were concentrated in specific districts.

“If there is terrorism and an emergency is needed in 12 districts, then why is governor’s rule across the whole province?” he said at a news conference in Islamabad after the government’s briefing.

Taimur Jhagra, a PTI leader and former provincial finance minister, rejected the government’s allegations.

“Of course the provincial government was fighting terrorism. We own the fight against terrorism individually and collectively. If the issue was terrorism, then Balochistan should have had a state of emergency before KP,” he told Al Jazeera.

PTI says Afridi, the chief minister until Sunday, and other party leaders are under arrest.

“We know the CM, the provincial president, Junaid Akbar, the speaker, Babar Swati, and some other leaders have been detained. The government has not revealed where they are,” Jhagra said.

Naqvi had also indicated on Sunday that PTI figures could be detained.

“Definitely, them or whoever else is needed for law and order, to maintain it, we will take into protective custody. But those among them who are wanted will be arrested, and everyone else will be released as soon as law and order improves,” Naqvi said.

Tarar, relaying Naqvi’s position at the same news conference, said some PTI figures had already been taken into preventive custody.

PTI says several provincial ministers and lawmakers were detained even before Sunday.

Internet monitor NetBlocks reported late on Sunday that network data showed a major disruption to connectivity in parts of the province.

District administrations closed schools and colleges in Peshawar, Mardan, Swabi and Nowshera on Monday.

Meanwhile, in Punjab province, Imran Khan’s sisters Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi have been held in custody since September 20-21, under a public order law that allows preventive detention for 30 days.

Provinces have been placed under governor’s rule at least eight times since 1949. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, then known as the North West Frontier Province, faced it in 1975 and 1994.

Because Zardari acted without a resolution from the provincial assembly, the Constitution requires both houses of Parliament to approve the emergency within 10 days, by October 21.

Sessions of the National Assembly and the Senate have been called for Tuesday.

The emergency must also be placed before a joint parliamentary sitting within 30 days. It lapses after two months unless approved by the joint sitting.

Once approved, however, the Constitution sets no fixed end date. The emergency remains in force until it is revoked or a majority of the total membership of both houses votes against it.

Governor’s rule under Article 234 has a separate limit. Parliament can extend it in two-month increments, for a maximum of six months in total.

“The emergency provisions allow the executive to suspend certain fundamental rights, and there is no fixed time limit for how long an emergency can continue, allowing for prolonged federal control,” Hosain said.

Gohar said PTI would challenge the measures in the courts and the assemblies.

“We have not formally called off the long march at all. Our struggle, as I told you, will absolutely continue,” he said.

articles.title: I’ve spent 25 years at historic museums. Smithsonian should tell of America’s greatness
articles.summary: The Smithsonian Institution faces a pivotal debate over how to balance America's achievements and shortcomings ahead of the 250th anniversary.
articles.body: The Smithsonian Institution is sometimes called the nation’s attic. That description is inadequate. An attic stores things. The Smithsonian does something far more consequential: It helps Americans understand who we are. That responsibility carries particular weight as the United States celebrates its 250th anniversary and the Smithsonian prepares for new leadership. The transition comes amid an intense debate over how the Smithsonian presents American history. A White House review criticized the National Museum of American History, arguing that ideological concerns have displaced an understanding of history as a shared national inheritance. Smithsonian leaders and historians have defended the institution’s scholarly independence and warned against allowing political power to dictate how history is told. The answer cannot be choosing one of those impulses and ignoring the other. TRUMP V. SMITHSONIAN: A TIMELINE OF HOW THE WHITE HOUSE FIGHT OVER 'WOKE' HISTORY UNFOLDED Outgoing Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch recently said the Smithsonian must show both the light and the dark. He has also described America as an ideal as much as a place — an aspiration toward liberty, fairness, justice and equality. But has the Smithsonian been telling the American story fairly? SUPREME COURT CHIEF JUSTICE PRAISES OUTGOING SMITHSONIAN LEADER WHO WAS UNDER PRESSURE FROM TRUMP ADMIN The harder question is one of proportion: How should America’s national museums put the light and the dark together into an honest account of the country? I have spent much of the past quarter-century helping govern museums and historic institutions in Virginia. That experience has convinced me that historical integrity requires more than factual accuracy. It requires proportion, context and perspective. HISTORIAN BLASTS SMITHSONIAN'S ACTIVISM SHIFT AFTER FIRST VISIT IN OVER A DECADE: 'COMPLETELY DIFFERENT PLACE' America’s national museums should tell our history honestly, including our shortcomings, contradictions and occasions when Americans failed to live up to the principles proclaimed at the nation’s founding. But those failures should not become the organizing principle through which the American experience is understood. SMITHSONIAN'S NATIONAL MUSEUM OF AMERICAN HISTORY PROMOTES 'EXTREME POLITICAL ACTIVISM,' WH REPORT ALLEGES Viewed in proportion, the American story is extraordinary. A collection of colonies declared that human beings possess rights governments do not grant. Americans then built an enduring constitutional republic around representative government, individual liberty and the rule of law. Those ideas changed human history. The nation they produced survived civil war, expanded freedom and political participation, welcomed generations of immigrants, became an industrial and scientific power, defeated fascism and Soviet communism and put human beings on the moon. America’s national museums should tell our history honestly, including our shortcomings, contradictions and occasions when Americans failed to live up to the principles proclaimed at the nation’s founding. When America fell short of its founding principles, succeeding generations repeatedly returned to those principles to demand the nation do better. There is an important distinction between examining America critically and teaching Americans to regard their country cynically. A great national museum should be capable of the former without succumbing to the latter. Museums inevitably make choices: which objects to display, which stories to emphasize and which context visitors receive. Individual facts can be accurate while their cumulative presentation leaves a distorted impression. LEGAL EXPERT CALLS FOR SMITHSONIAN LEADERSHIP OVERHAUL OVER ‘SELF-LOATHING’ PORTRAYAL OF HISTORY: ‘IT’S BILE’ The Smithsonian should resist any interpretive approach that begins with contemporary political or ideological categories and works backward through history to validate them. History should illuminate today’s debates, but the past deserves to be encountered on its own terms. Nor can the answer be replacing one political orthodoxy with another. WATCH: SMITHSONIAN DIRECTOR ADMITS SHE SEES HISTORY AS ‘TOOL’ OF ‘SOCIAL JUSTICE’ AFTER EXPLOSIVE HEARING The Smithsonian has endured presidents and Congresses of both parties. Its credibility rests upon scholarship, independence and public trust. Americans should never believe exhibits in their national museums are rewritten whenever political power changes hands. James Smithson envisioned an institution devoted to the "increase and diffusion of knowledge." Two centuries later, the Smithsonian holds objects that belong to all of us: General George Washington’s uniform. President Abraham Lincoln’s hat. The Star-Spangled Banner. The Wright Flyer. Harriet Tubman’s hymnal. The Greensboro lunch-counter stools. The Apollo 11 command module. They tell a remarkable story of aspiration, struggle, achievement and progress. No curator owns that story. Neither does a president, political party, academic movement — or generation. We hold it temporarily in trust. That principle matters especially during America’s 250th anniversary. This milestone should invite reflection. But reflection is not national self-reproach. Our semiquincentennial should not become a 250th-anniversary wake, principally devoted to cataloging America’s shortcomings while treating its achievements as qualifications or afterthoughts. There is too much worth celebrating. Visitors should leave the Smithsonian knowing America’s history more fully. They should understand our shortcomings and contradictions, but also our achievements. They should leave impressed by what Americans built, moved by what Americans sacrificed, grateful for what they inherited — and challenged to preserve and improve it. They should even leave proud. Pride in one’s country is not the enemy of historical understanding. Properly grounded in truth, it can be one of its products. The Smithsonian need not tell Americans what to think about America. It should give them the artifacts, scholarship, context and perspective necessary to understand the inheritance that belongs to them. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Tell the hard stories. Tell the great ones, too. Trust Americans with both. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP After 250 years, the American story remains unfinished. The Smithsonian’s responsibility is to preserve it faithfully, interpret it honestly — and ensure the next generation understands why it remains a story worth celebrating.

articles.title: Why CJI declined to meet Rahul Gandhi, Kharge amid protests against Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant had declined a request from Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha leader of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant had declined a request from Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge for a meeting to discuss issues arising from the ongoing protests in Delhi.He said the matters are already pending before the Supreme Court and discussing them administratively would violate the principle of separation of powers.In a letter dated October 11, the CJI advised the two Opposition leaders to approach the Supreme Court through the judicial process instead of submitting a memorandum on the administrative side. He also assured them that any petition filed on the issues would be heard at the earliest possible opportunity in accordance with the law.The request concerned allegations of irregularities involving the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the Election Commission of India, alleged arbitrary arrests of students, the closure of metro stations and the cancellation of trains amid protests in the national capital.READ ALSO: How Jantar Mantar became Delhi's designated protest site and what changes nowExplaining his decision, CJI Surya Kant said the issues raised by Gandhi and Kharge were “already sub judice before the Supreme Court of India.”“Therefore, convening a meeting to discuss pending cases would wholly contravene the principle of Separation of Powers, an intrinsic facet of the basic structure doctrine of the Constitution of India, and would be incompatible with the established ethics and judicial propriety,” the CJI said.He also clarified that the Supreme Court did not have administrative powers to address the concerns raised in their letter, but could examine them through its judicial jurisdiction.“However, in the exercise of our jurisdiction under Article 32 of our Constitution, along with other plenary powers, including that of judicial review, we are duty-bound to consider on the judicial side the gravamen of issues affecting the citizens of India,” he said.The CJI reiterated the Supreme Court’s commitment to protecting citizens’ fundamental rights and said they could seek their enforcement through the legal process.“Supreme Court of India reiterates its commitment to preserve and protect the Fundamental Rights of every citizen of India and they are entitled to seek enforcement of such rights at all hours through the procedure known in law. It would thus be more appropriate on your part to invoke the judicial powers of the Supreme Court of India, instead of submitting a memorandum on the administrative side,” he said.Pointing to the court’s schedule, CJI Surya Kant said matters involving similar issues were listed for hearing on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. He invited the Opposition leaders to file a petition on Monday, either physically or through the court’s e-filing facility.“If so advised, you may submit your petition on Monday, either physically at the Supreme Court of India, between 10:30 A.M. and 04:30 P.M., or alternatively, by utilising the e-filing option, which permits filing at any time and on any day. You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law,” he said.Gandhi and Kharge had sought an appointment with the CJI amid Opposition protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities, including what Congress has described as “vote chori”.Kharge said in a social media post on Sunday that the Opposition would continue its fight and that he and Gandhi had written to the CJI seeking a meeting.“We will continue our fight. Tomorrow, we are also going to meet CJI. I have written a letter, and Rahul Gandhi has also written a letter. We have scheduled a meeting between 4-5pm, during which we will apprise him of the situation... Chaos is being created in the country by home minister and PM, and everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed,” Kharge said.The CJI’s response leaves the Opposition leaders free to pursue their concerns through a formal petition, with the court indicating that related matters could be taken up through judicial proceedings.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: New Jersey mental health directory launches
articles.summary: It provides information about a range of services to support mental health, officials say.
articles.body:
A new online directory bringing together mental health services across Jersey has been launched.

The Mental Health Directory provides information about a range of services designed to support islanders' mental health and wellbeing.

It aims to help people understand what support is available, find services that meet their needs and access help for themselves or others, health officials said.

Andy Weir, managing director of the Health and Care Service, said: "Many of us need support at times. Islanders have told us that finding the right support can be difficult."

Weir added: "The new Mental Health Directory brings together information on mental health services in Jersey in one place, helping people find the support they need.

"Seeking support can be an important first step, and the directory is designed to make that step easier by helping Islanders understand what help is available and how to access it."

articles.title: Pope Leo to be hospitalized Tuesday for surgery to remove a lung nodule
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a hospital Tuesday morning to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests, the Vatican said Monday.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a hospital Tuesday morning to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests, the Vatican said Monday. The timing of the procedure was confirmed after the 71-year-old American pontiff had a full day of meetings, audiences and appointments. The Vatican press office also said no particular issue precipitated the tests, denying Italian media reports suggesting an inflammation had prompted the medical check-up. Leo revealed the discovery during his Sunday noon prayer and said he was following doctors’ advice to remove the nodule “in the coming days.” The Vatican predicted a weeklong recovery. It was business as usual at the Vatican on Monday, with Leo presiding over six private audiences, including with the head of the U.S. military chaplains, Archbishop Timothy Broglio, and one group audience. He also made three appointments, and the Vatican released a letter he had penned to the outgoing dean of the College of Cardinals. In the afternoon, he was expected to rejoin a weeklong conference he convened on ministering to families. Leo’s surgery marks the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. It was significant because the pope himself revealed the news, in perhaps the most public way possible: at the end of his Sunday noon blessing, with thousands of people in St. Peter’s Square. The Vatican has for centuries zealously guarded the pope’s health and has often sent out confusing information, or none at all, about papal illnesses. Pope Francis tried to change that by being upfront about his frailties and musing on his eventual death. But even during his pontificate, information was tightly controlled. Leo’s decision and reveal suggested an unusual level of transparency by the American pope. A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3 centimeters (1 inch) that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and oftentimes surgical removal is recommended to ascertain whether it is cancerous since performing a lung biopsy by needle can be difficult. Oncologists say if the nodule turns out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis is “excellent” since it will have been removed at an early stage.
