articles.title: Deadly Saudi airport strikes mark major Mideast escalation
articles.summary: Fears of intensifying conflict were growing in Saudi Arabia on Monday after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis launched multiple strikes on Riyadh’s airport over the weekend, killing 13 people and wounding hundreds.
articles.body: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Fears of intensifying conflict were growing in Saudi Arabia on Monday after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis launched multiple strikes on Riyadh’s airport over the weekend, killing 13 people and wounding hundreds. “What is clear is we remain on a strong escalation ladder,” said Adam Baron, a fellow at New America, a Washington, D.C.-based think tank, who follows Yemen and the wider Gulf region. More than 300 people were injured when the kingdom’s main international airport was attacked Saturday, marking a major escalation in the Houthi rebel group’s campaign against the world’s leading oil exporter and key U.S. ally in the region. Among the victims were one American, as well as four citizens of Saudi Arabia, two Bangladeshi nationals, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Palestinian, a Syrian and one Sudanese national. The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia later said on Sunday that an Indian national injured in Saturday’s attack had died. Video capturing the Saturday attack showed a packed airport before the flash of an explosion sends people running for safety as debris falls on them. The airport remained shut Monday. The impact of the attacks were felt at the WPC Energy Congress in the capital Monday, with several top energy executives dropping off the event’s schedule. The chief executives of Exxon Mobil, TotalEnergies, Shell, Chevron and BP had all been expected at the event, which started Sunday, but were no longer on the agenda that conference organizers released early Monday, Reuters reported. The energy giants did not immediately respond to requests for comment from NBC News. “You know this country is safe and that we hold your protection at whole heart,” Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said, according to Reuters, as he opened Monday’s session of the gathering held just miles away from Riyadh airport. But, he added, “our gathering here does not mean the risk is gone.” He said the stepped-up fighting was serious and that the kingdom’s response must be “equally serious.” “There is no way that somebody will break our back. We are like a phoenix,” he separately said. “We come out of the ashes all the time and every time.” Fighting on the ground in neighboring Yemen is also intensifying, with the Houthis expanding their operations along its Red Sea coast and around the Bab el Mandeb, a key shipping route connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. Saudi Arabia and the Houthis began fighting in 2015 after the kingdom entered Yemen’s civil war on behalf of the internationally recognized government. A period of relative calm following a 2022 ceasefire was shattered in July when the Houthis resumed attacks after accusing Saudi Arabia of firing on the Sanaa airport as a plane from Iran was attempting to land. Baron said the latest attacks — the deadliest by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia in more than a decade — could have a “galvanizing effect” on Washington and other international actors, including Pakistan and Turkey, which recently reached a joint defense agreement with the kingdom. “As these attacks are growing stronger and stronger, on the one hand, it’s increasing the hurt on the kingdom, but it’s also increasing assessments for many that that there has to be some strong effort to degrade the Houthis and restore deterrence,” Baron said. Washington faces mounting pressure. President Donald Trump on Saturday said he was still weighing whether to join in Saudi Arabia’s military operations against the Houthis. “We may. We’re gonna look at it,” he told reporters. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.” After sweeping gains by Houthi forces in Yemen last month, Trump said the rebel group had contacted the U.S. to stress that it doesn’t “want to fight with us” and would “much prefer not having us involved.” While the skies over Riyadh were empty Monday after flights in and out of the capital were canceled, roads were full of traffic as residents tried to get back to normal life. And in the early hours of Sunday, road crossings at the border with the United Arab Emirates were largely deserted. “With the Houthis, we knew that they could hit Riyadh airport, but it’s almost about the precision,” Baron said. “There’s a great degree of anxiety in terms of ... living in a world where you can just have random armed groups hitting airports, right?”

articles.title: Drumcree: Garvaghy Road residents fail in bid to challenge Parades Commission decision
articles.summary: Judges said their decision was confined to the lawfulness of the decision, not in deciding whether or not the march should occur.
articles.body:
The Garvaghy Road residents have failed in a bid to challenge the Parades Commission's decision to allow the Drumcree parade to walk down the predominantly nationalist road, the Court of Appeal has ruled.

Judges said their decision was confined to the lawfulness of the decision - it was not deciding whether or not the march should occur.

Lady Chief Justice Dame Siobhan Keegan said the ruling was decided before the secretary of state banned the parade on Friday .

Residents had argued the commission's decision was flawed over how it weighed up the potential for disorder when it approved the parade for the first time since 1998.

The commission said the parade should start earlier than the Orange Order wanted and with fewer people, but could go ahead for the first time in 28 years.

On Monday, the Lady Chief Justice found the Parades Commission properly dealt with a police assessment on the potential risk of disorder and gave adequate reasons for its decision.

"This application for leave to appeal has no reasonable prospect of success," she held.

What is the Garvaghy Road dispute all about?

Four key takeaways from the Drumcree dispute so far

Earlier at the High Court , an Orange Order challenge to a decision to ban the Drumcree parade was delayed after Northern Ireland's police chief Jon Boutcher was added to the case.

The Portadown Orangemen want to overturn the Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant's intervention on Friday night , which came after he received advice from the chief constable.

Spokesperson for the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition Breandán Mac Cionnaith said the decision was "very academic", considering Sir Chris has "banned the march in question".

He said that discussions on whether to take further legal action will take place with solicitors "later on".

"The ban is in place, that's what we sought, we have prevented the march and we will be back again to prevent further marches," he told reporters outside court.

He added that there are "questions there about the parades commission" and said they will have to "provide a full explanation" on their decision to allow the march.

Mac Cionnaith also acknowledged there was "continued uncertainty" as the Orange Order would "more than likely" plan other marches along the Garvaghy Road.

He said he was hopeful changes to the commission in the new year would "bring a fresh focus and a fresh view" to procedures.

Also speaking outside court, loyalist activist Jamie Bryson said the "lawlessness and the lawbreakers have been defeated", adding that "the law is clear".

"The Portadown District had a legal right to walk the Garvaghy Road.

"The objections to it were unarguable as a matter of law.

"They have lost twice in the high court, twice in the court of appeal - how many times do we need to beat them before they will abide by the law?"

"For those 11 residents' groups dug up from the 1990s to threaten parades, go ahead, go ahead, open them all up," Bryson added.

"Because see after the court of appeal decision today, we're going to be walking all of those traditional routes again."

Bryson said the ruling was "humiliating" for the chief constable and the NI Secretary, who he said the Orangemen would be challenging next week over the decision to ban the parade.

The Drumcree parade dispute began in the mid-1990s and it almost derailed the peace process at the time.

Violence related to the dispute resulted in riots, roadblocks and murders.

When the Orange Order was prevented by police from walking down the route in July 1995 there was a tense stand-off. It was the same for the next three years.

The Parades Commission began operating in 1998 to regulate parades and try to defuse tension around marches.

Its decision not to allow a march down the Garvaghy Road that summer has been challenged by the order for the past three decades.

Last month the Parades Commission decided that the march could go ahead on 27 September with restrictions in place after its original decision to stop the march was overturned in court.

That morning, up to 1,000 people - including nationalist politicians - blocked the road, preventing Orangemen marching from Drumcree Church a mile to the west.

Since then there have been repeated attempts by the Orange Order to walk the route, but they have been stopped by police.

Residents maintained a constant presence on the Garvaghy Road, but that ended on Friday when the NI Secretary Sir Chris Bryant banned the parade following advice from the PSNI chief constable.

articles.title: ‘Dear Surya Kant ... ’: Congress Keralam unit’s post asking CJI to 'resign' draws BJP fire
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday accused the Congress of threatening Chief Justice of India Surya Kant after the opposition party's Keralam unit posted a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday accused the Congress of threatening Chief Justice of India Surya Kant after the opposition party's Keralam unit posted a social media message asking the CJI to "resign."Follow live updatesIn a post on X, the Congress’s Keralam unit wrote: “Dear Surya Kant, if law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it.”The post, which has now been deleted, was in response to the CJI’s statement, as quoted by PTI, that the matter of law and order was not his domain. This was in response to the unprecedented security curbs imposed by Delhi Police amid ongoing protests in the capital seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Reacting to the Keralam Congress' post, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari wrote on X: “Anarchist Congress! This is a big insult to Constitution of India! Congress is threatening Chief Justice of India! Congress thinks Gandhi Vadra Parivar is above the Constitution! Congress hates Indian democracy & independent Constitution bodies!”BJP MP Nishikant Dubey tweeted: "After the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, and Chief Election Commissioner, now Maharaja @RahuGandhi ji has demanded the resignation of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court as well. According to sources, after this resignation, Rahul Gandhi ji will become Prime Minister, Sharjeel Imam President, Abhijeet Deepke Vice President, Priyanka Gandhi ji Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, and Khalistani Pannu Chief Election Commissioner. Soros will be India's ambassador in America."On Monday, leaders of the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc moved the Supreme Court against the Election Commission (EC), naming the poll body, Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as respondents.The petition has 11 petitioners, including Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, among others.The petition was filed after the Chief Justice of India declined the opposition’s request for a meeting to submit a representation on alleged “vote chori” (vote theft) by the EC for the ruling BJP. CJI Kant later explained, “I received a letter yesterday (Sunday) regarding a meeting request, and I responded to it last night, outlining the reasons why I will be unable to meet.”“The Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone. Any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected body is welcome. Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law,” he added.CEC Kumar has come under scrutiny over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and a media report claiming a rift between him and the two election commissioners.Congress calls X post 'completely incorrect'Reacting to the social media post, Congress MP and party spokesperson Pawan Khera said the Congress "disagrees" with the statement, calling it “completely incorrect.”Also Read | 'Absolute faith in judiciary': Congress rejects Keralam party unit's post on CJI Surya Kant“We completely disagree with this position, whoever has done it. It is completely incorrect. We have absolute faith in the judiciary of this country and respect the highest court. That is exactly why we approached the highest court, as we have full confidence in the judiciary,” Khera told ANI.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Israeli academic and Al Jazeera contributor Ori Goldberg dies at 50
articles.summary: Goldberg was a regular Al Jazeera contributor and died after a long battle with colon cancer, his family said.
articles.body:
Israeli academic and independent analyst Ori Goldberg has died at the age of 50, his family has said.

His eldest daughter Avigail confirmed his death after a long battle with colon cancer in a statement on Goldberg’s X account on Sunday.

“In one sentence, he was the best dad in the world. But you can’t really describe him in one sentence, and I don’t think I’ll have the courage to try,” she wrote.

In a separate post on Goldberg’s X account, his eldest son, identified as Dave, said his father was “the light where things looked dark”.

Goldberg was a frequent contributor to Al Jazeera’s website where his opinion pieces focused on Middle East affairs.

In his final piece for the Qatar-based media network last month, he wrote about Israeli authorities’ reaction to the award-winning documentary NAZA , by Yuval Avraham and Rachel Szor.

In a memorable piece titled Israel is imploding in December 2025, he explored whether Israel could be losing its status as regional hegemon while the Israeli state and society become increasingly dysfunctional.

“An international coalition, led by the United States with the participation of Qatar, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, is gradually removing Gaza from Israel’s control, as well as pressuring Israel out of its territorial escapades in Syria and Lebanon,” he wrote.

In another piece from the same month titled Netanyahu will win again he explained why the Israeli prime minister’s supporters would likely vote for him in a 2026 election.

“He is ‘their’ man, the one who represents them against the elites who feel the country is theirs by right. He alone, through his audacity and cunning, took the fight to Israel’s enemies and brought them to their knees.” he wrote. “[Netanyahu] is the one who broke the paradigm that put Israel at the mercy of the world. Israel now does as it wishes, and those desires are for Israel alone to articulate”.

Goldberg also appeared regularly on Al Jazeera English news and current affairs shows including Inside Story.

He received a PhD in History from Tel Aviv University in 2008 and wrote his dissertation on the role of religious experience in the creation and application of Iranian Shia revolutionary discourse during the second half of the 20th century.

He received many awards and scholarships, including a fellowship at the Mellon Foundation from 2013 to 2015.

articles.title: Your dryer does need to be cleaned — here’s how to do it and what to use, according to experts
articles.summary: For the best way to clean a dryer, and to learn more about how often to do it, I talked to home cleaning experts for their recommendations and guidance.
articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like whether bath sheets are actually different from towels. It makes sense that you may never think about cleaning your dishwasher or washing machine, since unlike the stuff you wash in them, you don’t interact with them much. The same could be said for your dryer, but just like the aforementioned appliances, your dryer does need to be cleaned from time to time. Cleaning home appliances that you use nearly every day keeps them functioning properly and saves you money. Think about it: A few dollars for products and an hour of your time now spares you from paying a repairperson later, or worst case scenario, needing to replace your dryer altogether. So to find the best methods and products for cleaning a dryer, I spoke to multiple home cleaning experts for their recommendations, which I talk more about below. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for cleaning a dryer Before you start the process you’ll want to grab some highly-rated materials to help you get the job done. All of the products below are either recommendations from our experts or editors, and/or have at least a 4-star average rating on Amazon from 500 or more shoppers. Some selections are also based on products we’ve covered before. This kit comes with an 8.5-inch bristle brush that lets you clean in and around your dryer vent to remove dust and lint. The rod you attach to the brush is available in several lengths up to 30 feet and it’s bendable, making it easy to clean in the crevice of the dryer vent without much hassle. The kit also comes with a 4-inch wide bristle brush that you can use to clean the inside of the dryer’s exhaust duct, which is a wide, hose-like structure attached to the back of your dryer and the wall. You can also attach the wide brush to a power drill and use it to lift away lint from the inside of the duct, according to the brand. Since the cleaning process involves touching and removing a lot of dust and dirt, you may also want to use gloves, which the kit doesn’t include. This set includes a bendable brush, hose attachment and an adapter that allows you to use the vacuum you already have to clean the inside of your dryer vent, as well as the dryer lint screen and the inside of the exhaust duct. While many vacuums come with their own hose and crevice attachments, some of them aren’t always the right length, so they won’t always be able to get into the vent. With this attachment kit, you can connect it to your vacuum’s hose or crevice tool, essentially extending its overall reach. Plus, this allows you to clean the duct thoroughly without having to put your hand in it. This popular dishwashing spray is one of NBC Selected’s most recommended cleaning products, and it’s not just for dishes. It’s great for cleaning many surfaces around the home, including screens and filters from a dryer vent or window air conditioner. Spray it on the dryer vent screen after removing it, rinse it with water and allow it to dry before putting it back in the vent. It has a light clean fragrance which I love and it doesn’t contain any harsh chemicals that attach to your hands, like bleach or peroxide. This set includes one spray bottle and three refills. When I wrote a guide on how to clean stainless steel appliances, I recommended microfiber cleaning clothes like these. The cloths are great for cleaning many surfaces, including the steel exterior of your dryer, because they’re soft and they don’t leave scratches or marks. Plus, microfiber cloths can help buff the outside of your appliance and give it a luxe, shiny appearance. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans loves using microfiber cloths for wiping the outside of appliances made from stainless steel. How to clean a dryer Follow the expert-recommended steps below for cleaning your dryer. Consider using the products above to help. While you don’t have to clean the entire dryer that often, it’s most important that you regularly clean the lint trap (the screen in the lining of the door) regularly, according to Ryan Knoll, founder of home cleaning company TidyCasa. Aside from simply wiping away the lint, you can do things to clean it more thoroughly, he says.To clean the lint trap and the compartment it slides into, use the crevice and hose attachment tool from your vacuum or a hose attachment kit, like the Holikme Dryer Vent Cleaner Kit with Lint Vacuum Attachment & Brush, to clean the lint on the screen. Then use it to clean the inside of the compartment. You can also use a long bristle brush, like the one included in the Holikme kit, to clean the lint on the inside of the compartment.To clean the dryer vent and exhaust duct, you’ll need a long bristle brush and a wide brush that you can attach to a long rod, such as from the Holikme Dryer Vent Cleaner Kit, to be able to reach the inside of the duct. The kit includes a nylon rod that attaches to a power drill, so that you can put the brush attachments inside the duct and rotate it to lift the lint before using the vacuum and hose suck it out. How often do you need to clean your dryer? Cleaning the screen that traps lint frequently is most important, according to Knoll. “Clean the lint trap every time before or after you use the dryer,” says Knoll. “Clean the dryer vent itself every two to three years. We’re talking deep hose clean-out, either sucking lint out or pushing it through the vent.” The dryer vent includes the exhaust duct (the silver hose-like structure made from aluminum) on the back. Can a dryer cause a fire? Yes, the lint that collects in and around the dryer vent and lint trap can block air from the dryer and, in addition to preventing your clothes from drying, can lead to a fire, according to Becky Rapinchuk, owner of cleaning brand and site Clean Mama*. This is why she recommends cleaning the screen frequently, including with warm water and soap. “Vacuum the lint trap housing regularly. Clean the dryer vent hose or duct at least once or twice a year to keep airflow strong and drying times short,” she says. “Wipe the drum occasionally, and clean the moisture sensors (inside the drum) with a little rubbing alcohol on a cloth to remove residue that causes inaccurate dryness sensing.” *Any product recommendations in this story were made independently of Rapinchuk, who we only consulted for guidance. We did not ask her for product recommendations. How do you know if your dryer needs to be cleaned? Make a note of how your clothes feel after drying them once — they may still be damp after drying for a long time. “If your dryer isn’t drying your clothes as well as it used to, that’s a good sign it needs a cleaning,” says Knoll. This is because lint is trapped on the screen of the dryer vent, which stops air from getting through and drying clothes properly, according to Knoll. articles.title: Disagree with the judge. Don't mock the office
articles.summary: \"Dear Surya Kant, If law and order is not your domain, resign now.
articles.body: "Dear Surya Kant,If law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it."This is not a letter from an angry citizen. It was (now removed) a post from the verified handle of the Keralam unit of the Indian National Congress, addressed to the Chief Justice of India.Read it twice. The tone is not disagreement. It is command.The provocation is easy to trace. Asked by reporters about the protests in Delhi, the CJI said it was a matter of law and order, not his domain. A day earlier, he had declined a meeting sought by Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, the Leaders of Opposition in both Houses. The issues were pending before the court, he said, and a meeting would breach the separation of powers and judicial propriety.One may question his choice of words. One may argue that liberty is very much the court's domain, and that policing and fundamental rights overlap. That is a legitimate debate. It belongs in the courtroom, in Parliament, on the editorial page.But whatever the reason, this language is unacceptable. A grievance is not a licence for contempt.Dropping the title and addressing the Chief Justice by name is not casual. It is deliberate, meant to diminish. "Resign now" is an order no political party has the standing to give. A Supreme Court judge can be removed only through the process in Article 124(4): proved misbehaviour or incapacity, an address passed by both Houses by a special majority, and an order of the President. The Constitution made removal difficult precisely so that judges would not have to fear the displeasure of those in power, or those seeking it.Then comes the most revealing line: "We will find your replacement who can handle it."Who is "we"? No political party finds, appoints or replaces a Chief Justice. By settled convention, the outgoing CJI recommends the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court, and the President appoints. A party has no role in it.Yet the sentence is written as if appointing Chief Justices were routine party business. Perhaps that is a habit of memory. The seniority convention has been set aside only three times, in 1964, 1973 and 1977, all under Congress governments. The last two, when Justice AN Ray superseded three senior judges and Justice MH Beg superseded Justice HR Khanna, are widely seen as punishment for inconvenient judgments. The party may know the territory, but it should not sound nostalgic about it.None of this places judges above criticism. A democracy needs scrutiny of its courts, and sharp scrutiny at that. Disagree with a remark. Question a judgment. File a petition. Make the argument in public, with facts.What a democracy cannot afford is the habit of mocking an institution every time it does not deliver what one wants. Today's opposition is tomorrow's government, and the reverse. The court is the umpire for both. A side that heckles the umpire whenever a decision goes against it is not protecting the game. It is wearing it down, and one day it will need that umpire itself.Those who hold up a copy of the Constitution at every rally should also read what it asks of them. Article 121 bars even Parliament from discussing the conduct of a Supreme Court judge, except on a motion for removal. If the Constitution restrains the sovereign legislature, a party's social media handle can surely restrain itself.The Constitution is not only a list of rights. It is also a code of conduct. Carrying it is easy. Honouring it is the harder part.Disagree with the judge. Respect the office.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Iran-Saudi talks on Yemen’s Houthis: What’s in it for Tehran?
articles.summary: Tehran seeks dialogue in Yemen conflict, warning a military solution risks complicating the volatile regional situation.
articles.body:
Iran has offered to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi group after a series of deadly attacks on the kingdom, raising questions about Tehran’s diplomatic calculations as fighting intensifies across the region.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spoke with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, on Sunday, in their first publicly reported contact since the Iran-aligned Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The diplomatic outreach comes after strikes on Riyadh’s international airport over the weekend killed 14 people and wounded hundreds, while Saudi-backed forces continued their offensive against the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah, in Yemen.

The talks also come against the backdrop of the wider US-Israel war on Iran, with Tehran potentially seeking to avoid being dragged into another confrontation.

“Tehran is an ally of Ansar Allah and has influence with the movement, although it does not control its decisions,” Negar Mortazavi, senior fellow at the Washington, DC-based Center for International Policy, told Al Jazeera.

“By offering to facilitate talks with Riyadh, Iran is positioning itself as an indispensable party to a broader regional settlement.”

So what discussions are happening between Riyadh and Tehran, and why is Iran offering to facilitate talks?

What did Iran and Saudi Arabia talk about?

According to the Saudi state news agency, the two foreign ministers discussed the recent escalation in the region and efforts to reduce tensions. Iran’s Foreign Ministry also confirmed the development.

Following the discussions, Araghchi on Sunday warned against pursuing a military solution to the conflict and offered Tehran’s assistance in facilitating dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

“Insisting on a military approach and disregarding a political solution would only further complicate the situation,” Araghchi said, according to Iran’s Foreign Ministry.

On Monday, ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei reiterated Tehran’s willingness to mediate, saying Iran was deeply concerned about developments in the Arabian Peninsula.

“We absolutely do not want hostilities and war to continue between two Islamic countries,” Baghaei said, urging dialogue to resolve the conflict.

What is Iran’s stance on the war in Yemen?

Iran has repeatedly called for a diplomatic settlement to Yemen’s conflict and says it supports a political solution rather than continued military action.

Tehran backs the Houthis, who control Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, and other parts of the country.

The armed group forms part of the Iran-aligned “axis of resistance”, which also includes Lebanon’s Hezbollah and armed groups in Iraq.

Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, has led a military coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government since 2015.

Baghaei said on Monday that the conflict served Israeli interests, framing a negotiated settlement as preferable to further fighting.

What is the latest in the Yemen fighting?

Fighting has intensified in Yemen, after the internationally recognised government’s forces announced Operation Dawn of Yemen on October 4 to reverse recent Houthi territorial gains, including the capital, Sanaa.

Government forces, backed by Riyadh, have reported advances near the strategic Bab al-Mandeb strait, a vital international shipping route. However, competing battlefield claims remain difficult to independently verify.

The Houthis have responded with missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and other targets.

Two strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Saturday and Sunday killed 14 people and wounded more than 300. The casualties included foreign nationals from Bangladesh, Pakistan and Palestine.

The escalating violence has also disrupted commercial flights, businesses and schools in Riyadh, underlining the growing economic and civilian consequences of the conflict.

UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg warned on Friday that Yemen had returned to “full-scale war”, with civilians bearing the brunt of the attacks.

Why is Iran willing to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis?

Iran’s offer to facilitate talks between Riyadh and the Houthis could be an attempt to strengthen Tehran’s diplomatic position and secure a wider regional agreement that extends beyond Yemen.

“I think Iran is trying to turn Yemen from a military liability into a diplomatic asset,” Andreas Krieg, a Middle East security analyst at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera.

He said Tehran recognises that Saudi Arabia is struggling to reverse Houthi territorial gains, particularly around Taiz and Bab al-Mandeb, despite intensifying its military campaign.

“Araghchi’s offer is an attempt to position Iran as part of the solution to a crisis in which it has also helped sustain the problem,” Krieg said.

Analyst Mortazavi, meanwhile, said Iran’s diplomatic outreach is part of a broader effort to link the conflicts unfolding across the region.

“The larger political objective is an informal non-aggression arrangement between Iran and its allies on one side and the United States and its regional partners on the other,” she said.

Such an agreement, she argued, would require an end to hostilities across multiple fronts, including Yemen and Lebanon, rather than a settlement confined to the US-Iran conflict.

Moreover, academic Krieg said there was also an important “Saudi dimension” to the discussions.

“Riyadh is increasingly uncomfortable with its dependence on Washington, frustrated by the limited American willingness to intervene in Yemen and reluctant to become dependent on the UAE again,” he said.

“Iran sees an opportunity to demonstrate that engagement with Tehran can deliver something Saudi Arabia’s traditional security partnerships have struggled to provide.”

There are also economic considerations, the analysts noted. Iran is under significant pressure from the US blockade, while Gulf countries are gradually recovering their energy exports to pre-war levels despite Iranian disruptions.

“Offering Riyadh a way out of Yemen potentially gives Iran leverage well beyond the Yemeni theatre, particularly in negotiations over Hormuz, sanctions relief and the wider regional security architecture,” Krieg said.

However, Krieg cautioned against overstating Iran’s influence over the Houthis, who have their own political ambitions and demands.

“Ansar Allah is not simply an Iranian proxy awaiting instructions,” Krieg said. “Its leadership has its own political ambitions, increasingly sees itself as a regional military actor and believes its recent territorial gains have strengthened its negotiating position. Iran can facilitate talks and potentially influence the intensity of escalation, but it cannot simply order the Houthis to surrender their gains around Mocha or Bab al-Mandeb.”

For Mortazavi, the broader message is that regional security cannot be addressed in isolation.

“Ultimately, Tehran’s message is that regional security cannot be divided,” she said. “Saudi Arabia cannot obtain security from attacks, while Iran and its allies remain under military and economic pressure.”

articles.title: Nearly four years after engineers rated Coconut Island’s only pedestrian bridge in serious condition, an 8,000-pound county excavator helped collapse it; Hawaii now faces up to $22 million to restore access
articles.summary: For years, the short walk to Coconut Island in Hilo was part of the rhythm of visiting the waterfront.
articles.body: For years, the short walk to Coconut Island in Hilo was part of the rhythm of visiting the waterfront. Then the bridge became a warning sign: fencing, closure notices and an increasingly uncertain future for one of the area’s most familiar public spaces. Now, after a section of the bridge collapsed under an 8,000-pound county excavator, restoring that connection could cost Hawaii County as much as $22 million, states an online report by the Beat of Hawaii.The incident has brought renewed attention to a structure that engineers had already identified as badly deteriorated years before the collapse, raising questions about maintenance, equipment use and how a relatively modest repair estimate became a multimillion-dollar replacement proposal.A warning that came years earlierAccording to the Beat of Hawaii, a January 2022 inspection found extensive deterioration in the bridge’s concrete and exposed, corroding steel. Engineers classified the pedestrian crossing as being in serious condition and estimated repairs at about $1.35 million, including design and permitting.Despite its condition, the bridge remained open to pedestrians with restrictions on large gatherings and maintenance vehicles. The county proposed about $2.5 million for bridge repairs that year and announced handrail work in March.What remains unclear is whether the recommended structural repairs were completed before the eventual collapse. There is also no clear evidence that the engineering assessment specifically approved the use of an excavator weighing roughly 8,000 pounds on the aging structure.The collapse changed everythingAs per the online report, when the bridge gave way in November 2025, the excavator was being used as part of county operations. County officials had already been discussing a design contract for rehabilitation or replacement, but the collapse accelerated the need for a solution.The county has also pointed to the history of heavy equipment crossing the bridge. The structure had reportedly been reinforced in the early 2000s and carried no posted weight limit. Yet the earlier engineering assessment had documented significant deterioration, leaving questions about how equipment continued to use the crossing and whether everyone involved was aware of its condition, adds the online report.For residents, the consequences extend beyond engineering reports and construction budgets. Coconut Island, known traditionally as Mokuola or the healing island, holds deep cultural significance for Native Hawaiians. It was regarded as a place of healing and refuge, with longstanding traditions connecting the island to protection, family and wellbeing.Why the price tag has soaredThe financial jump has become one of the biggest points of concern. The earlier $1.35 million figure represented repairs to the existing structure, while the current proposal involves building a new permanent crossing.Hawaii County now estimates roughly $20 million for a permanent replacement and as much as another $2 million for temporary access. The larger proposal also includes seawalls, utilities and other improvements, making it difficult to isolate the precise cost of the bridge itself, claims the online report.Officials have indicated that federal funding could potentially cover much of the replacement expense, but a final award and detailed funding breakdown have not yet been established.A possible return in 2027There is finally a tentative timeline for reopening the island. Temporary bridge construction could begin as early as January 2027, with pedestrian access potentially returning by June or July, subject to permitting and construction.For Hilo residents and visitors, reopening would restore access to a small but meaningful part of the waterfront. Coconut Island sits near Banyan Drive and Queen Liliuokalani Gardens, both of which remain accessible. The bridge may have been only a short crossing, but its absence has exposed a much longer story about deferred maintenance, historic infrastructure and the price of waiting until a familiar public connection becomes impossible to ignore.Image Courtesy: Beat of HawaiiYou use AI every day. articles.title: Zelenskyy accuses Putin of defying Trump's ceasefire push, sends pointed message to White House
articles.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy accuses Vladimir Putin of attacking Ukraine's gas infrastructure hours after Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire.
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Fox News on Monday that Russia continued attacking Ukraine's energy infrastructure despite President Donald Trump's announcement of what he called an immediate energy ceasefire, accusing Vladimir Putin of rejecting Washington's peace efforts and calling for greater pressure on Moscow. "We are ready today for energy ceasefire, as President Trump said. But I'm not sure that Putin is ready because even after yesterday's messages from the president about energy ceasefire, Putin attacked our gas infrastructure," Zelenskyy told Bill Hemmer in a live interview on "America's Newsroom." Asked whether Ukraine would honor the ceasefire, Zelenskyy answered, "Of course," insisting that Kyiv had already refrained from striking Russian energy facilities overnight. TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE "We didn't attack any energy objects on the territory of Russia because President Trump said that there will be an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. And we didn't attack, but Russia attacked our gas stations, energy infrastructure, infrastructure and other things," he said. The Ukrainian leader described the attacks as Putin's response to Trump's initiative. "It was his answer to President Trump. He attacked our energy infrastructure," Zelenskyy said. "The communication from Russia was very clear that they don't know anything about energy ceasefire." Trump announced Sunday on Truth Social that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate halt to attacks on energy facilities. But Moscow has not confirmed accepting such an agreement, and the precise scope of Trump's proposal remains disputed. According to Axios reporting Sunday, a White House official said the proposal initially focused on halting attacks on oil refineries, with a broader ceasefire covering power plants and electricity grids potentially following. The official acknowledged that Russia had not yet agreed. UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE Zelenskyy pushes back on Trump's refinery demands During the interview, Hemmer pressed Zelenskyy on whether Ukraine would halt attacks on Russia's extensive oil-refining network, which has become a point of contention between Washington and Kyiv amid rising global fuel prices. Zelenskyy argued that a ceasefire limited to refineries would fail to address Ukraine's greatest vulnerability: its electricity supply. "When we speak about energy ceasefire, it means only one thing: that they don't attack our energy infrastructure, and we don't respond to their energy infrastructure. This is called energy ceasefire." Asked again whether Ukrainian forces would refrain from targeting Russian refineries, Zelenskyy gave a conditional commitment. "If Russia will not attack our energy, we will not attack the energy," he said. Trump has repeatedly criticized Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries, arguing that they contribute to higher fuel prices. On Friday, he announced an agreement with Russia to release diesel supplies to the U.S. and global markets, a decision that drew criticism from lawmakers concerned about providing Moscow with additional revenue. Zelenskyy challenged Trump's assessment of what is driving diesel prices, pointing instead to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. "Everybody understands that the price on diesel doesn't depend on our attacks on diesel in Russia," Zelenskyy told Hemmer. "Everybody understands that it depends on the blocking of Hormuz Strait." NEW RISK FOR US CONSUMERS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS THREATEN A SECOND MAJOR OIL CHOKEPOINT 'Only our people can change' Ukraine's president The interview also exposed tensions over Trump's calls for Ukraine to hold new presidential elections. Over the weekend, Trump criticized Zelenskyy and suggested Ukraine needed a new president, arguing that Kyiv had missed opportunities to reach a negotiated settlement with Russia. "If President Trump wants to change the leader in Ukraine, he has to know that only our people can change," Zelenskyy responded. The Ukrainian president said he was willing to organize an election but argued that voting remained impossible without a substantial pause in hostilities. "I'm ready for elections. Really, we need a minimum 60 days for security of infrastructure to prepare for elections," he said. Zelenskyy described continuing Russian drone and missile attacks as an immediate threat to voters. "We are speaking about thousands of drones, ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, how can people vote?" he asked. "It's not even about the law. The law is very important. But we speak first of all about security." He also said he last spoke directly with Trump in New York during the U.N. General Assembly in late September. ZELENSKYY TO SEEK OFFRAMP FOR YEARS-LONG RUSSIA WAR IN UN SPEECH AFTER TRUMP REVEALS PEACE DEAL IS CLOSE Russian attacks continue as Moscow resists ceasefire The interview came after another series of Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities and residential areas. Ukraine's charge d'affaires in Washington, Denys Sienik, said Sunday that Russian forces struck a power plant in Kyiv, disrupting electricity and water supplies, before attacking a thermal power plant in Kharkiv following Trump's announcement. "In total, over the course of the week, Russia struck electricity generation and transmission facilities more than 200 times," Sienik wrote on X on Oct. 11, 2026. East2West News agency reported Monday that three civilians — a 16-year-old boy and two women, ages 19 and 51 — were killed in a strike near a grocery store in the Kharkiv region. The agency also reported that five people were wounded in an attack on a residential high-rise. In Pisochyn, a woman described witnessing the bombardment of a power plant shortly after Trump's announcement, according to East2West. "We believed the statement that they wouldn't strike energy infrastructure," she said. "Just ten minutes after that promise was made, there were already five strikes." The agency also reported a Ukrainian strike on a Russian military base in occupied Khrustalnyi, in the Luhansk region, where three large fires were reportedly visible. The damage and casualty figures could not be independently confirmed. Reuters separately reported Monday that Russia continued striking Ukrainian energy targets despite Trump's announcement, while Kyiv maintained that it had refrained from attacking Russian refineries. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, meanwhile, rejected the prospect of a 60-day ceasefire to facilitate Ukrainian elections, arguing that European countries would use the pause to replenish Ukraine's weapons supplies. "I don't think he deserves a respite," Lavrov said Monday, according to the BBC. UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS Trump's Russian diesel deal draws criticism The latest developments have intensified scrutiny of Trump's decision to ease restrictions on Russian diesel, which critics argue could provide Moscow with additional revenue while it continues its military campaign. Carrie Filipetti, executive director of the Vandenberg Coalition and a former deputy assistant secretary of state during Trump's first administration, questioned whether the arrangement would undermine U.S. leverage over Putin. "Both Russia and Ukraine seemed surprised by the announcement of an energy ceasefire, and unsurprisingly, Russia has continued to attack Ukrainian energy facilities — reportedly as recently as a few hours ago," Filipetti told Fox News Digital. "Putin probably hopes the new diesel deal — which directly undermines recent US legislation calling for an increase in tariffs and sanctions against Russian energy — will discourage President Trump from holding Putin accountable for these continued violations and attacks." Filipetti argued that Russian energy revenue remains a critical source of financing for Moscow's war effort. "If we want a real ceasefire, paying directly for Putin's war machine through this new diesel deal is not the way to do it," she said. "President Trump's goal of a ceasefire could be a real win — but it's only going to happen if we stop the diesel deal." Morgan Murphy, former head of public diplomacy for the Special Presidential Envoy to Russia and Ukraine, offered a different assessment, defending Trump's efforts to secure a negotiated settlement. "President Trump has consistently prodded both sides toward the only realistic outcome — negotiation," Murphy told Fox News Digital. "Both sides are losing right now: Ukraine doesn’t have the combat power to retake seized land, and Russia is destroying its future demographics with every passing day." Murphy argued that prolonging the fighting would only deepen the human toll: "Trump is right to push for a ceasefire. An endless war of attrition benefits only the makers of weapons and coffins." In his Fox News interview, Zelenskyy also emphasized the human cost of the war, saying Russian strikes were killing between 20 and 30 civilians a day, a figure Fox News has not independently verified. "We want to end this war as quickly as possible," he said. "Ceasefire is a good first step from both sides. This is very important." articles.title: Singers go underground as Cornwall tin mine prepares to reopen
articles.summary: A mine echoes to the sound of a choir singing deep underground as plans continue to reopen it.
articles.body:
The sound of music has echoed around a Cornish tin mine which is getting a new lease of life after a group of 21 shanty singers tested out its acoustics.

The Cadgwith Cove Inn Singers performed 25 fathoms (150ft, 45m) below ground at South Crofty in Pool after being given a tour of the mine.

They sang in an area where owner Cornish Metals has been tunnelling to allow ore-handling facilities as it prepares to reopen the mine and create 300 jobs .

Singer Bentley Orchard, who has also worked in mining, said the experience "was phenomenal" and the acoustics "were resounding, reverberating", as if "the old miners were throwing the words back at you".

The invitation followed a gathering at the pub where the singers perform regularly to mark the 28th anniversary since the mine closed .

The Cadgwith Singers had to go down eight at a time in a transport cage to part of the mine where the company has been extracting water and using as a training ground for their next generation of miners.

Cornish Metals ground production manager Steve Tarrant said it was a "steep learning curve" for the next generation of miners being trained there but he was proud of their progress.

The company said the visit "was a wonderful reminder of the traditions that continue to unite our communities".

The government invested £28.6m in 2025 in plans to reopen the mine.

A new workshop and stores facility opened in September 2026, providing maintenance, engineering and storage facilities for the mine.

articles.title: Parents protest proposed merger of Rohtas primary school
articles.summary: Parents in Rohtas protest proposed merger of Rupibandh Primary School, citing distance, highway safety risks and poor infrastructure despite Rs 25 lakh sanction.
articles.body: Sasaram: The education department’s proposed merger of Rupibandh Primary School with other schools in Rohtas district has triggered protests from parents, who fear the move could jeopardise their children’s access to education and safety. The school, which caters to Classes I to V, has 82 students studying in a single 20x15-foot room with just one blackboard, reflecting a severe shortage of basic infrastructure.Established in 1996 in Chitauli panchayat of Kochas block, the school has four teachers, including headmaster Shashank Kumar Tiwary, and a cook. The lone classroom also doubles as the headmaster’s office and storage space for midday meal supplies, utensils and other materials. The school also lacks a proper urinal, playground and drinking water facilities.Parents have opposed the proposed merger with other schools, arguing that shifting students elsewhere would not address the underlying infrastructure problem.According to the parents, one of the proposed alternative schools, Chitaini Primary School, is around 6km away, while Middle School at Bardhauti Kala is approximately 1.5km from Rupibandh. However, children would have to cross a busy national highway to reach the nearer school, which parents said posed an accident risk. They said similar concerns existed over access to the other proposed school.The parents have also lodged a complaint with the headmaster, warning that they would not send their children to school if the merger goes ahead. They said the authorities should improve the existing school’s infrastructure instead of imposing additional hardships on students from disadvantaged families.According to Shashank Kumar Tiwary, headmaster of Rupibandh Primary School, the state govt last year sanctioned Rs 25 lakh for the construction of additional classrooms at the school, but work could not begin because of the non-availability of land. The unresolved land issue has left students studying in cramped and inadequate conditions. Tiwary said a meeting of the School Education Committee would be called soon to discuss the proposed merger.Meanwhile, DPO (Establishment) Rajanish Upadhyay said reports had been sought from the headmaster and the assistant block education officer on the proposed merger to ensure the smooth conduct of teaching activities.However, parents maintained that any decision should take into account the distance to alternative schools, road safety risks and the urgent need for adequate classrooms.chamaria_alokad@yahoo.co.inYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: ECR beefs up security at 300 locations with focus on passenger safety
articles.summary: East Central Railway boosts Durga Puja security at 300 locations with drones, scanners, CCTV, QRTs and 24x7 surveillance at major stations.
articles.body: Patna: The East Central Railway (ECR) has beefed up security measures at around 300 locations across its jurisdiction in view of the commencement of Durga Puja with a special focus on crowd management, passenger safety and prevention of untoward incidents at railway stations.According to ECR principal chief security commissioner-cum-IG RPF Amaresh Kumar, as part of the enhanced security arrangements, Railway Protection Force (RPF) has deployed advanced surveillance equipment including drone cameras, handheld metal detectors, door frame metal detectors, baggage scanners, solar-powered standalone cameras and body-worn cameras. “These gadgets will help security personnel keep a close watch on passenger movement and identify suspicious activities within railway premises,” he said.In addition, the RPF personnel have been deployed at foot overbridges (FOBs), circulating areas, ticket booking counters and waiting halls to regulate passenger movement and prevent overcrowding. CCTV cameras and RPF intelligence personnel are also being used to maintain round-the-clock surveillance at sensitive locations, the RPF IG said.Quick response teams (QRT) have been kept ready to deal with any emergency situation, while special security squads have been formed to strengthen vigilance during the festive rush. RPF is also monitoring crowd movement to ensure the smooth entry and exit of passengers at major stations, Kumar said, adding Patna Junction, Rajendra Nagar Terminal, Danapur, Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga, Samastipur, Barauni and other crowded stations are under 24x7 surveillance.Railway security personnel have been directed to remain alert throughout the festive period with particular attention to crowded platforms and other vulnerable areas. articles.title: Supermodel Erin O'Connor praises Wolverhampton teens' upcycled catwalk creations
articles.summary: Erin O'Connor judges young Wolverhampton designers creating fashion from discarded clothes.
articles.body:
Teenagers who transformed unwanted clothes into catwalk-ready fashion have won praise from supermodel Erin O'Connor after showcasing their creations at a Wolverhampton fashion show.

More than 100 students presented original designs made from donated and pre-loved garments at the event at Wolverhampton's Mander Centre.

The winning outfit, created by Sebastian and Railijs, both 13, and Lucian, 14, featured a grey blazer decorated with colourful upcycled materials including plastic bottle caps, fabric scraps, ribbons and patterned textiles.

The teenagers spent a month transforming discarded clothing through sewing, repair and redesign before taking to the runway to present their creations.

O'Connor, originally from the Brownshill area of Walsall, who has walked for Prada, Chanel and Alexander McQueen, returned to her home region to judge the show, assessing the creativity and transformation of the outfits and sharing tips with students on how to walk the runway.

"It was a privilege to be part of the event and to see first hand the creativity, passion and innovation shown by young people from my local area," she said.

"The future of fashion depends on its ability to become more sustainable, and it was incredibly inspiring to see these students leading the conversation and finding imaginative ways to reimagine and upcycle clothing."

Railijs said he was "surprised" but "very happy" that his team had come first.

"All the things we added to the outfit represent how polluted the world is," he said.

"I'm thinking about whether I'd like to become a designer in the future."

The event was run by social enterprise Reinvntd Community Interest Company (CIC) with support from Save the Children's Young People Climate Fund.

A Save the Children ambassador for 15 years, O'Connor said the charity's work supporting children in the UK and around the world was "more important than ever".

"Future Threads is a wonderful example of what can happen when young people are given the opportunity to develop new skills, express themselves creatively and make a difference in their communities," she added.

Maya Patel, founder and director of Reinvntd CIC, said the project was "so much more than fashion".

"We've seen students go from not knowing how to thread a needle or sew on a button to creating more than 30 amazing upcycled garments and confidently showcasing their work on a public catwalk," she said.

articles.title: Meet Harrison Nott, 16, from Essex, England, who skipped college after his GCSEs to grow the towel business he started in his bedroom in 2023, now generating over £750,000 in annual revenue
articles.summary: A 16-year-old entrepreneur from Essex, UK, has chosen not to attend college to focus on his towel business, CoolTowel, which he started in his bedroom in
articles.body: A 16-year-old entrepreneur from Essex, UK, has chosen not to attend college to focus on his towel business, CoolTowel, which he started in his bedroom in 2023. Harrison Nott's venture has generated more than £750,000 in revenue this year, driven by a surge in demand during Britain's summer heatwaves. His journey received a major boost when he won the Alibaba.com CoCreate Pitch competition, beating 15,000 entrepreneurs worldwide and securing a £150,000 prize. Former England footballer Rio Ferdinand, one of the judges, was impressed by the teenager and later invested in his business. Harrison says CoolTowel has recorded around 80,000 sales through TikTok Shop and Shopify this year, although the company is yet to turn a profit.CoolTowel sells reusable cooling towels that work through evaporation. Users wet the towel, wring it out and snap it to activate the cooling effect. According to SWNS, demand soared during the summer heatwaves, with Harrison claiming the business generated £100,000 in revenue in a single night after selling out its stock.He later introduced pre-orders and says the company sold £600,000 worth of stock in one week, taking its annual revenue beyond £750,000.Why he decided against going to collegeDespite passing his GCSEs, Harrison decided against attending college after discussing the move with his parents. He acknowledged that leaving the conventional education route was difficult, especially as his friends were moving on to college.“I really do value school, but me and my parents made the decision that it would be best for me to not go to college,” he said, as quoted by SWNS.He added, “It is like stepping away from the norm. Not going to college is burning the bridge.”Rio Ferdinand's investment and a trip to Los AngelesFerdinand later met Harrison in London to discuss his business plans and decided to invest in the venture. The former footballer has also helped the teenager build connections and explore opportunities for growth.Harrison subsequently travelled to Los Angeles, where he met Ferdinand and celebrities including James Corden and former Manchester United striker Javier Hernandez.“Rio is a lovely person. He is not arrogant at all,” Harrison said, adding that he admired Ferdinand for his efforts to support young entrepreneurs.Business challenges and future plansDespite the impressive revenue, Harrison has faced stock shortages, problems with TikTok Shop's handling of pre-orders and copycats allegedly using his face in advertisements. He believes platform-related issues cost him an opportunity to capitalise further on the summer heatwaves.Advertising campaigns, affiliate commissions and other expenses have also prevented the business from turning a profit.“It was all a punch in the face at once. It has been very good, with a very terrible last few months,” he said.However, Harrison remains optimistic about the future. “It is not just a business in my bedroom anymore, it is a brand that is helping people properly,” he said.He added that the business has stock and other assets and hopes to break even as it continues to grow.You use AI every day.
